legalNotice.title: How legal-text versions work
legalNotice.body: The privacy notice, the terms and the declaration are written and approved here. Every approved version is frozen for good — a correction is the next version, started from its text, never a rewrite. An approved version may be deleted only if nobody relied on it — a signature, a registration's acknowledgement, or an event that uses it — and it is not the version in force right now. Registration is refused while no privacy notice is in effect, and no place can be confirmed while no declaration is.

journey.title: The registration's journey
journey.heldKept: deadline passed, the place is kept while nobody waits
journey.legend:
The six steps of a registration:
– 1 · Form sent — the person filled in the registration form.
– 2 · Email confirmed — the address is confirmed: with the link from the email, or by staff at the desk.
– 3 · Place held — has a held place (or is on the waiting list, if not yet).
– 4 · Declaration signed — signed the declaration, online or on paper.
– 5 · Place confirmed — the registration is complete, with a place and a declaration.
– 6 · Present at the race — came to the desk on race day and picked up the number.
The figure in the column shows how many steps the registration has reached.

errors.LEGAL_DELETE_NEEDS_REASON: Type a reason. It is the only thing left after the deletion.
errors.LEGAL_TERMS_ACCEPTED: Nothing was deleted: this version of the terms now has registrations or signed declarations from the time it was in force, and neither records which version of the terms was accepted. You can withdraw it instead — it stays on the record and is offered to nobody.
errors.UNDER_MINIMUM_AGE: Nothing was registered: by the birth date typed, this person is not yet {age} old on the day of the race, the minimum age for this event. Check the date with them.
errors.NEON_QUOTA_BELOW_USAGE: The limit was not sent: a new limit must be above what this period has already spent plus the margin, or it would stop the database the moment it is saved. The spend and the smallest limit are written under the box.
errors.NEON_QUOTA_UNCONFIRMED: Nothing changed: a new or changed limit on production needs the confirmation box ticked — when it is reached, the site stops until the next period.
errors.NEON_UNCONFIGURED: Nothing changed: NEON_API_KEY or NEON_PROJECT_ID is missing on this environment (SETUP.md §33).
errors.NEON_KEY_FORBIDDEN: Neon refused the change: the key in NEON_API_KEY reads the project but may not modify it — most likely a personal key whose owner may only view the project. A project-scoped key may: in Neon, the organization's Settings → API keys → Create new → Project-scoped, on this environment's project — an organization Admin creates it, and Neon gives it Editor access to that one project. A personal key works only if its owner is an Admin of the organization or an Editor on the project. Put the key in NEON_API_KEY on the environment's Vercel project and redeploy. The figures above the form are what Neon holds now.
errors.NEON_BUSY: Neon was working on another change to the project and did not take this one. Try again in a minute; the figures above the form are what Neon holds now.
errors.NEON_REFUSED: Neon refused the values sent. The figures above the form are what Neon holds now; if the size chosen is above what the plan allows, choose a smaller one.
errors.NEON_UNREACHABLE: Neon did not answer (or answered with something the page cannot read). The figures above the form are what Neon holds now; try again in a minute.
errors.NEON_QUOTA_REMOVAL_UNCONFIRMED: Nothing changed: removing production's limit needs the same confirmation box ticked — with no limit, production has no spending cap at all.
errors.WAITLIST_FULL: The places and the waiting list are full, so nothing changed. Try again once a slot on the list frees up.
errors.NO_WAITLIST: Every place is taken and the event has no waiting list, so nothing changed.
errors.WALK_IN_LEFT_UNCONFIRMED: The person was entered but could not be confirmed: the last place went at that very moment, and the waiting list had no room either. Their registration stays unconfirmed and no email was sent to them. Confirm it on paper once a place frees up; otherwise it lapses on its own when the confirmation link runs out (under “Deadlines”, on the Emails page).
errors.NO_RECIPIENTS: Nothing was sent: nobody is in the chosen group right now. Choose another group.
errors.MESSAGE_UNKNOWN_PLACEHOLDER: Nothing was sent: {names} is not a field the platform can fill in this message. The fields you can use are listed under the boxes.
errors.SAMPLE_VALUE_IN_EMAIL: The text contains the sample value “{value}” — use {placeholder}.
errors.SAMPLE_VALUES_IN_EMAIL: The text contains sample values, not fields: {found}. Use the fields in their place.
errors.BIB_NUMBER_TAKEN: That number is already somebody's at this event (given, held, or worn by an erased registration). Pick another number from the box and try again.
errors.WALK_IN_BIB_TAKEN: The person was entered, but somebody at the desk gave that number away a moment ago, so their registration stays unconfirmed and no email was sent to them. Find them in the desk's list and press “Confirm here” with another spare number.

editor.startsAtHelp: Local time of the event ({timezone}). For a race this is the gathering time.
editor.raceStartsAtHelp: When the gun goes, if that differs from the gathering time. Leave empty when there is only one time.
editor.mapUrlHelp: Optional. The meeting point on Google Maps or any other map. It must start with https://.
editor.coordinatesHelp: Optional: latitude, longitude — e.g. 45.6427, 25.5887. Copy them from Google Maps: right-click the point → the first line. Used only for the weather, when the map link does not carry them (a short link, a venue's page).

weatherPlace.map: The weather is read for the point in the map link ({coordinates}).
weatherPlace.typed: The weather is read for these coordinates ({coordinates}).
weatherPlace.club: The weather is read for {place} ({coordinates}): the map link carries no coordinates and none are typed.

editor.locationHelp: The place, as you would tell a friend: a name, a street, or both — in Romanian and in English, each for its own language's page. If it is called the same in both, press “Same name in English”: while the two say the same, what you type in Romanian is written in English too.
editor.locationEnglishLeftBehind: The English box still says “{place}”. If the place has moved, change it here too.
editor.placeToBeAnnouncedHelp: Turn it on when the place is not settled yet. The event can be published anyway: the page, the cards, the calendar, the share picture and the emails say “Location to be announced soon”, and the place, the address, the map and the programme's places appear nowhere. What you fill in below, in both languages, is kept, unpublished. When you announce the place, turn the switch off and save — it appears everywhere at once.
editor.placeUnpublished: Not published while the location is to be announced.
editor.featured: Lead the site with this event
editor.featuredHelp: Only one event can be featured. The previously featured one loses the flag automatically.
editor.specialHelp: An edition apart — an anniversary, a charity run, a race the club joins somebody else at. Shown with a badge on the card and on the page. Any number of events may be special, including one date of a series; the mark does not travel to the other dates.
editor.saveCoversSettingsOnly: Your save changes the settings only; the texts are the editor's.
editor.liveWarning: Published: every save appears on the site at once, in both languages.
editor.acknowledgeLive: I understand that I am editing published content.
editor.acknowledgeLiveHint: Tick that you understand you are changing published content to be able to save.
editor.slugHelp: The page address, in lowercase words joined by hyphens. It can only change before the first publication.
editor.slugLocked: The page has been published, so its address stays as it is.
editor.costHelp: What a participant pays. The platform does not collect money itself — the fee or the donation happens directly, with the organiser or at the link below. Leave "Not stated" when this has not been decided yet. A donation is the participant’s choice: if the place is given only once paid, choose "Paid" and add the payment link.
editor.costAmountHelp: For example "50 lei". Required for a paid event.
editor.costPaidUrlHelp: The link where payment is made. Must start with https://.
editor.costDonationUrlHelp: Required. The link where the donation is made, on another site. Must start with https://.
editor.discountNoteHelp: What discount members get and how they use it — the code, until when

fields.title: Title
fields.excerpt: Summary — shown on the page, on the listing card and in shares
fields.checklist: What to bring (one line, in the emails and the calendar)
fields.body: Content — shown on the event page, under the title

editor.sharedFieldHelp: The same in both languages. Filled in once.
editor.excerptHelp: One or two sentences: what the event page, the listing card (with a picture, if you put one in) and the shares carry. Required before publication.
editor.excerptEmpty: (required before publication — press to write it)
editor.programmeHelp: The day by the hour, one row each: kit pickup, the briefing, the start, the cut-offs, the awards. Shown as a list on the event page, repeated in the reminder email, and each row is its own entry in the calendar file. Every row starts on the event's day; a row with no time and no text is ignored. If you change the event's start date, the rows' dates move with it. Leave “Where” empty when it is the event's own place.
editor.rulesHelp: Optional, in both languages or neither. The race rules — what is allowed, what is not, how the kit is collected, the deadlines. Shown on the event page under “Rules”; the declaration and the emails point there.
editor.checklistHelp: Optional, in both languages or neither, at most 300 characters: “race number, water, a jacket”. It goes in the confirmation email, the reminder and the calendar entry.
editor.typeHelp: A group run is simply turned up to: no registration, no participants, no programme. A race has all of them; a hike, a coffee, an equipment test and another event may take registrations; an external event is somebody else's — its registration is on their page.
editor.endsAtHelp: Optional. Leave empty when the club has stated only a start.

night.label: Night event
night.autoLine: Automatic: on {day}, starts at {start}, sunset at {sunset} — {verdict}
night.autoLineDawn: Automatic: on {day}, starts at {start}, before sunrise at {sunrise} — {verdict}
night.autoLineNoTime: Automatic: on {day}, sunset at {sunset} — pick the start time
night.autoLineNoDate: Automatic: pick the start's date and time under “Date and time”, and the answer shows here.
night.endLine: The start is before dusk, but the run lasts until {end} and reaches the dark — still a night event.
night.endLineProgramme: The start is before dusk, but the day's programme runs until {end} (its last row) and reaches the dark — still a night event.
night.series: In a series, each date follows its own day's sunset: the winter dates are night events, the summer ones are not.
night.help: Automatic: it is a night event when any part of it, from the start to the end, falls after dusk (the sun 6° below the horizon) or before dawn. The end comes from “Duration” or, without it, the day's last programme row. Shown on the event's card, page and calendar, and in the reminder email.

editor.registrationModeHelp: Registration here needs a declaration; registration elsewhere needs the organiser's link.
editor.capacityHelp: Leave empty for unlimited. It cannot be lowered below the places already taken.
editor.capacityWaiting: On the waiting list: {waiting}. If you raise the number, the new places are offered at once, in order, {offer} each.
editor.waitlistCapacityHelp: Leave empty for unlimited. 0 means no waiting list: once the places are gone, registration stops. It only counts with a number of places. Lowered below how many already wait, it removes nobody from the list — it only takes nobody new.
editor.registrationWindowHelp: Leave the opening empty and registration opens when the event is published; leave the closing empty and it closes when the event starts.
editor.declarationDocumentHelp: Chosen from the approved versions; the text is never edited here. A new version is approved under Legal documents.
editor.declarationNone: No approved declaration exists in this environment, so no event can take registrations here yet.
editor.participantList: Publish the participant list on the event page
editor.participantListHelp: Publishes the name and club of the confirmed participants who ticked “I want to appear on the participant list”; every other confirmed participant appears as “Participant (name hidden)”, with nothing about them, and the list says how many are confirmed in all. No email addresses. Once the privacy notice in force describes the stages, the list shows each registration's stage beside the name and also holds those who ticked and have not confirmed yet, then the waiting list; a cancelled or expired registration never appears. This is a disclosure of personal data: the approved privacy notice must describe it before this is switched on, and the save is refused while no privacy notice is approved and in force.
editor.externalHelp: Both only for an event registered elsewhere. The link must start with https://.
editor.deleteHelp: A duplicate is created as a draft, is never featured, and gets its own page addresses. Deleting is for an event nobody has registered for; archive the ones that happened.
editor.routeUrlHelp: Where the route can be seen — a Strava route or activity, or any other https:// link. Leave empty if there is not one.
editor.routeDescriptionHelp: Optional, in both languages or neither. Pit stops, climbs, what to expect — and a map if you have one (the picture button). Shown on the event page under “The route”, with the route link and the GPX and map links from “Links and files”.
editor.repeatHelp: Make this a standing series: the same details at a fixed interval, the time kept in the event's own zone, until a date or for ever. The next {horizon} are created now and the platform keeps creating the weeks that follow, each date its own event — cancel or move one without touching the rest. Each date gets an address with its day (“sunday-run-2026-10-04”). Dates are drafts unless you tick publish.
editor.repeatUntilHelp: Leave empty for a series without an end.
editor.repeatStopHelp: No new dates are made; the ones already made stay — you delete them from the events list.
editor.repeatStopped: The series is stopped: no further dates will be made.
editor.repeatPublishOn: New dates of the series publish automatically: the source is published, so every new date starts published already.
editor.repeatPublishWaiting: Automatic publication is on, but waiting: the source is not published right now, so new dates start as drafts until it is published again.
editor.repeatPublishOff: New dates of the series start as drafts — automatic publication is off. You publish them yourself, from the list or from each one's own editor.
editor.repeatPublishStarted: Automatic publication has been turned on: from now on, new dates of the series publish by themselves.
editor.repeatPublishStopped: Automatic publication has been turned off: new dates of the series stay drafts until you publish them.
editor.savedSeriesOne: Saved — also on {dates} of the series.
editor.savedSeriesMany: Saved — also on {dates} of the series.
editor.savedSeriesOfferedOne: Saved — also on {dates} of the series; places offered to the waiting list: {offered}.
editor.savedSeriesOfferedMany: Saved — also on {dates} of the series; places offered to the waiting list: {offered}.
editor.savedOffered: Saved — places offered to the waiting list: {offered}.
editor.placeAnnouncedLive: The location is announced: it now shows on the event page, the cards, the calendar and in every email sent from now on. People already registered are not emailed about it automatically; the reminder before the start will carry it, if the event sends one.
editor.placeAnnouncedDraft: The location is announced: it will show on every page once the event is published. Nobody is emailed about it.

scope.title: Save for:
scope.help: As in Google Calendar: only what you changed here reaches the other dates — a new time lands at that time on each date's own day; a date moved or cancelled on its own stays so unless the place or the status is what you changed. Each date's page address stays.
scope.countThis: The save changes this date only.
scope.countFollowing: The save changes {dates}: {first} and the following {rest}, until {last}.
scope.countTail: A date moved or cancelled on its own stays as it is.

editor.repeatWeekdaysHelp: This event's own day is always in the series; tick the others too — Wednesday, say, for a Sunday run. Only days after this event are made. Nothing ticked: the event's own day alone, at the chosen interval.
editor.createdWithSeries: The event and {dates} were created, as drafts. Tick them in the events list and publish them together.
editor.durationHelp: How long it lasts — 1 hour 45 minutes, say. The end is worked out from it. Leave both empty if none was announced.

coHostRows.name: Partner's name

coHostRows.labelEnError: Partner {p}, link {l}: the English label — write it in both languages or neither, at most {max} characters

The GPX track, the map, the extended rules, a form, the photo album, the results — a link to wherever the file lives: Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Strava, Garmin. Share the file with “Anyone with the link”, or runners meet a request for access. linkRows.urlError: Link {n}: the address must start with https://
linkRows.kindError: Link {n}: choose the kind from the list

linkRows.tooMany: Links and files: at most {max} on one event

editor.stravaEventUrlHelp: Optional. The event's address in the Strava club (strava.com/clubs/…/group_events/…), for those who RSVP there. A recurring Strava event keeps one address for every date, so the series inherits it from the source event; any one date can change its own.
editor.facebookEventUrlHelp: Optional. The event's address on Facebook (facebook.com/events/…), for those who say "Going" there. A Facebook event with several dates keeps one address, so the series inherits it from the source event; any one date can change its own.
editor.bodyHelp: Optional, in both languages or neither. The full description, with headings, lists and links — the day's programme, what to bring, where to park. It appears at the top of the event page, directly under the title; the short description stays on the card.
editor.confirmationOpensDaysBefore: Participation confirmation: asked how many days before
editor.confirmationDeadlineDaysBefore: …and due how many days before (0 = at the start)
editor.confirmationWindowHelp: A runner confirms by signing the declaration, any time after confirming their email: online, from the registration email, or on paper at the registration desk. At the first number of days before the start we email them to ask for the confirmation. Until the deadline the place is theirs; after the deadline the place goes to the next in line only if someone is waiting. With 0 as the deadline, the place does not lapse before the start. Whoever registers after the window has opened, or when the first number is 0 (as on the weekly runs), has {hold} to sign.

typeNotes.GROUP_RUN: Group run: people simply turn up — no registration, no participants, no programme.
typeNotes.RACE: Race: registration, a declaration, race numbers and a programme for the day.
typeNotes.HIKE: Hike: may take registrations and have a programme, when places are limited.
typeNotes.COFFEE: Coffee: may take registrations, to book the table, and have a programme.
typeNotes.GEAR_TEST: Gear test: may take registrations and have a programme.
typeNotes.MEETUP: Other event: the one-off, with a partner or for an occasion. May take registrations and have a programme.
typeNotes.EXTERNAL: External event: it is somebody else's, and registration happens on the organizer's own page.

editor.deleteBlockedByTest: Cannot be deleted: it has {count} registrations, all of them test data. Remove those first, under “Test registrations” above.
editor.bibsOnlyTest: Numbers are given to real, confirmed registrations only. Everything here is test data, which never gets a number — for a rehearsal, add a participant at the desk.
editor.bibStartNumberHelp: Usually 1. Use 100 or 500 to give each distance its own band — numbers are given in order of registration, counting up from here.

reminder.label: The reminder before the start
reminder.help: The email with the time, the place, what to bring, the QR code and the number, sent to everyone confirmed, once — and with it the last call to sign for anybody who has not yet. “As usual” is the club's setting ({lead}), under “Deadlines” on the Emails page.

editor.minAgeHelp: Reached by the day of the event. Under 18, a parent or legal guardian registers the runner, with their consent. 0 means no minimum age.

bibDesign.title: What the race number looks like
bibDesign.intro: What is printed on the bib, and how large. The same choices show in the preview on the “Numbers” page and on the A4 sheet you send to the printer.
bibDesign.headerImageSrc: A picture instead of the coloured band
bibDesign.headerImageSrcHelp: It runs the full width across the top. With one chosen, the band, the logo and the text on it are not printed — the picture is the header.
bibDesign.sponsorImageSrcHelp: Above the small print at the foot. Fitted without being stretched.

footer.title: Footer
footer.intro: The small print at the foot, in the order below. What does not fit on one line goes onto a second; what does not fit there either is cut with “…” — the preview shows exactly where.
footer.showEventInFooter: The event's name and date, when the header does not show them
footer.footerTextPlaceholder: e.g. Timing: … · Organiser emergencies: 07xx xxx xxx
footer.footerTextHelp: It is printed on every number and worn in public — do not write participants' personal data.

bibDesign.previewAlt: The race number as it would look with the current choices, for a runner named “Nume Prenume”
bibDesign.previewNote: The pictures are the ones already uploaded (the “Pictures” page). The preview above changes at once; the “Numbers” page and the PDF follow a save.

editor.bibColourHelp: The band across the top of the printed number, the one carrying the club's logo and the race. “The club's colour” unless you want a specific one.
editor.createdPublished: The event was created and published. It is on the site, in both languages.
editor.createdPublishedWithSeries: The event and {dates} were created and published.
editor.createdNotPublished: The event was created as a draft but could not be published. Missing: {detail}. Nothing you typed was lost — fill it in and press “Publish”.
editor.createdNotPublishedRole: The event was created as a draft. Publishing is the Administrator's — submit it for review.
editor.createdNotPublishedOther: The event was created as a draft but could not be published: {reason}

notice.count: Participants who would get the “Updated details” email: {count}, each in the language they registered in. notice.countNone: Nobody is registered for this date right now, so the box sends no email.
notice.countSeries: If the change also reaches other dates of the series, their participants are told too, once each, about their own date.
notice.noteHelp: Optional, in both languages or neither · plain text, at most {max} characters each. Each participant gets it in the language they registered in, under “A message from the organizers”; without it, the email goes only if the place, the date and time or the programme changed.
notice.cancelTitleCreate: You are creating the event as cancelled
notice.cancelIntroCreate: The event is created with the status Cancelled and shows so on the site if you publish it. No email goes out: nobody is registered for a new event.
notice.cancelReasonHelpCreate: Required, in both languages · plain text, at most {max} characters in each. It stays in the audit log, with your name.
notice.cancelIntro: The registrations stay as they are, as a record: nobody is withdrawn and no status changes. No more places are offered, no numbers are given and no automatic emails go out for this event.
notice.cancelReasonHelp: Required, in both languages · plain text, at most {max} characters each. Each participant gets it in the language they registered in; it also appears in the audit log, with your name.
notice.cancelNotify: Tell the participants that the event is cancelled
notice.cancelCount: Participants who would get the “Event cancelled” email: {count}. Messages including the club's copies: {messages} — they count against the Mailgun allowance ({allowance}).
notice.cancelCountNone: Nobody is registered right now, so no email goes out.

outcome.update: “Updated details” emails queued: {queued}. They go within minutes, each in the participant's language.
outcome.none: No email went out: the place, the date and time and the programme did not change, and the note for the participants was empty.
outcome.cancelled: The event is cancelled. “Event cancelled” emails queued: {queued}.
outcome.cancelledQuiet: The event is cancelled. The participants were not told, because the box was unticked.
outcome.cancelledNobody: The event is cancelled. It takes no registrations on this site, so there was nobody to email. The reason is in the audit log.

notice.countTest: Test registrations, which get the email too and are counted nowhere: {test}.

notice.noteEnError: What changed (English): write the note in both languages or neither, at most {max} characters
notice.cancelReasonRoError: Why the event is cancelled (Română): required in both languages, at most {max} characters
notice.cancelReasonEnError: Why the event is cancelled (English): required in both languages, at most {max} characters

editor.immediateActions: Immediate actions — they do not go through “Save”
editor.groupRunNoRegistration: A group run takes no registration — anybody simply turns up. Change the type under “What kind of event” to take registrations.
editor.groupRunNoProgramme: A group run has no programme.
editor.modeNoneSentence: The page says no registration is needed.
editor.repeatPublishOffHelp: Off: new dates are created as drafts; you publish them from the events list.
editor.repeatPublishDraftSource: While the event is a draft, new dates are drafts too.

groups.page: The event page, top to bottom

publication.createDraft: Created as a draft: nothing appears on the site until it is published.
publication.nothingMissing: Nothing is missing: the event can be published.

risk.place: Those registered know the place “{place}”. If you change it, tick “Tell the participants” under Save.
risk.programme: The reminder before the start repeats the programme and every row is a calendar entry; a change is one of those “Tell the participants” sends.

risk.status: Cancelling stops registration and, if you leave the box ticked, tells those registered with the reason written here.

queue.title: The registration queue
queue.holdsHelp: “Held” are the places kept while somebody signs the declaration ({hold}, or until the confirmation deadline for events further away than their window) or answers a waiting-list offer ({offer}). A hold past its deadline stays the person's — they can sign online any time, or on paper at the desk — and is released only when somebody is waiting for a place, when somebody registers whom the waiting list has no room for, or when the event starts. Free = places − confirmed − held, exactly the formula the public sees; while the waiting list is full, the public also sees the place of a lapsed hold as free, because the next person to register gets it.
queue.lineEmpty: Nobody is waiting. The list fills once the places are gone.
queue.lineNone: This event has no waiting list: once the places are gone, registration stops.
queue.interestTitle: Addresses waiting for the opening notice: {count}
queue.interestHelp: Left at "Tell me" on the event's page. Each gets one email on the job's first run after registration opens and is deleted with it. If somebody writes that they no longer want the message, type their address here: it leaves the list. The addresses themselves are not shown.
queue.interestRemoved: The address was removed from the notification list.
queue.interestNotFound: That address was not on this event's list. Check whether they wrote from another one.
queue.simulate: How to simulate the waiting list (not in production): set a small number of places in Settings, save, then add more test registrations below than there are places — the first take the places (held for {hold} each), the rest queue here, in order. Cancel a confirmed one, let a hold lapse (the maintenance job runs every 15 minutes) or raise the number of places and the first in line gets the offer; its email shows in the Outbox on that registration.

testRegistrations.explanation: Synthetic participants on reserved @test.invalid addresses, which can never receive mail. They go through the ordinary submission and confirmation path, so they occupy places and fill the waiting list exactly as real people do — and they are left out of the CSV export and labelled everywhere they are listed. Not available in production.

legal.readOnlyNotice: This version is approved, so its text is fixed: participants have relied on it. To change the wording, start the next version from this one — it opens prefilled, you edit, save the draft, read it and approve it. The old version stays exactly as it was.
legal.nextVersion: Start the next version from this one

pdf.draftNotice: DRAFT — unapproved version. The text below has no effect until it is approved and may still change.

legal.newFromIntro: Prefilled from version {version}. Change what needs changing, save the draft, read it, then approve it. Version {version} stays as it is.
legal.noTranslations: This version has no text yet.
legal.newFromTemplateIntro: Prefilled with the platform's text, the club's legal name and the contact address already written in. Left to fill, in angle brackets, in both languages: {blanks}. Read it all, save the draft, then approve it from its page.
legal.templatesIntro: Or start from the platform's text:
legal.tokensHelp: In the declaration only, these fields are filled in automatically for each person and event: '{{participant}}' (the registered name), '{{participantIdDocument}}' (their identity document, typed at signing), '{{guardian}}' and '{{guardianIdDocument}}' (a minor's parent or guardian and their document; a dash for an adult), '{{idDocument}}' (the declarant's document — the parent's, for a minor), '{{event}}' (the event's title), '{{eventDate}}' (its date), '{{eventLocation}}' (its place), '{{signedAt}}' (the moment of signing). legal.newIntro: You are writing a new version, not changing an existing one. It saves as a draft and is not public until you approve it.
legal.bodyHelp: A blank line separates paragraphs. A line starting with ## is a section heading. A link: [the words](https://…). A picture, on a line of its own: ![what it shows](https://…) — copy the address from Gallery → Pictures.
legal.keyLocked: The document cannot change after creation.
legal.editorWarning: This is the club’s legal text. Write or paste only wording the club has approved — never invent legal content.
legal.approveHelp: Once approved the text is public and can no longer be edited. A later correction means a new version.
legal.approveConfirm: I confirm the club has approved this text and it may become public
legal.legalVersionApproved: The version is approved and now public.
legal.termsRegistrations: Registrations while it was in force: {count}

startFrom.orBlank: Or write from nothing, in the form below.

tokens.title: The fields that fill themselves in
tokens.intro: Leave them exactly as they are in the text. The participant's and the event's — in the declaration only — are replaced at signing, for each person and each race; the four deadlines, in any of the three texts, with the values under “Deadlines” on the Emails page. The club's own facts are not here: those are already written into the text.
tokens.participant: The name the participant registered under
tokens.declarant: Whoever signs: the participant, or the parent or guardian for a minor
tokens.guardian: The parent or guardian when the participant is a minor; a dash otherwise
tokens.idDocument: The declarant's identity document (the parent's, for a minor), typed at signing — never scanned
tokens.participantIdDocument: The participant's own identity document — the minor's, for a minor — typed at signing. With it in the text a minor signs too, beside the parent; without it, only the parent signs
tokens.guardianIdDocument: The parent's or guardian's document when the participant is a minor; a dash otherwise
tokens.eventDate: The event's date, in its own zone
tokens.confirmationHours: How long the address confirmation link is valid, from “Deadlines”
tokens.holdMinutes: How long a place is held for signing, from “Deadlines”
tokens.offerHours: How long a waiting-list offer stays open, from “Deadlines”
tokens.reminderClause: The reminder as a clause with its comma, from “Deadlines”: the club's lead, noting that an event may choose its own; with no number when the club sends none by default, since an event may still send one
tokens.minimumAge: The event's minimum age, with its unit (“16 years”). On an event with no minimum age — on a group run, one of 18 or less — the sentence naming it is left out of the declaration
tokens.participantListStates: Privacy notice only: the three stages the public list shows beside a name, in quotation marks. With it in the notice in force, the public list shows each person's stage, those who have not confirmed yet and the waiting list; without it, only confirmed names
tokens.publicListPeriod: Privacy notice only: how long the public participant list stays up after the event, from “Deadlines”, unit included; after that the list closes by itself
tokens.newsletterTopics: Only in the privacy notice: the topics the news subscription on the contact page offers, in quotation marks. With it in the notice in force (in both languages), the contact page offers the subscription; without it, the subscription does not appear and no address is kept.

legal.removeBlockedReferenced: Can neither be withdrawn nor deleted: {signatures} signatures, {events} events and {acknowledgements} registrations depend on this version.
legal.removeBlockedCurrent: In force right now — it can neither be withdrawn nor deleted. Approve its successor first; then this one can go.
legal.deleteMeans: Deleting is permanent: the text goes entirely, and version number {version} stays retired for good.
legal.legalVersionErased: {phrase} has been deleted permanently. Its number stays retired: it will never be given to another version.

erase.title: Delete permanently: {document}, version {version}
erase.whatGoes: {document}, version {version}, in force since {date}, goes permanently: the text in both languages, the titles and the row itself. It cannot be recovered.
erase.numberRetired: Version number {version} stays retired for good. The next version of this document takes the next number, never {version} again, so a number people already ticked at registration can never end up on different words.
erase.auditOnly: One trace is left: an audit line with the document, the number, the date it took effect, who approved it, the SHA-256 of each language's text and the reason you type. The text itself is kept nowhere.
erase.nothingDepends: It can be deleted because nothing depends on it: no signature, no event, no registration — and it is not the text in force right now.
erase.termsNobodyAccepted: It can be deleted because nobody accepted it: it was in force {window}, and in that time no registration was submitted and no declaration was signed — and it is no longer the text in force.
erase.termsNeverInForce: It can be deleted because nobody accepted it: it was never the text in force.
erase.alreadyWithdrawn: You already withdrew this version, on {date}. Deleting is the second and final step: now it leaves the record as well.
erase.notWithdrawn: This version has not been withdrawn. If you only want it to stop being offered anywhere, withdraw it from the list instead: it stays on the record, with its text and its number. Deleting cannot be undone.
erase.phraseHelp: Type exactly “{phrase}” to confirm. Anything else stops the deletion.
erase.reasonHelp: It stays in the audit log. It is the only thing that survives the deletion.
erase.blockedDraft: This is a draft, not an approved version. Delete it from the list with the button on its own row, with no typed confirmation: nobody has seen it and its number was never given to anyone.
erase.blockedReferenced: Cannot be deleted: {signatures} signatures, {events} events and {acknowledgements} registrations depend on this version. What people accepted stays.
erase.blockedCurrent: This is the version in force right now. Approve its successor first; then this one can be withdrawn or deleted.
erase.blockedTermsAccepted: Cannot be deleted: while this version of the terms was in force, {window}, registrations were submitted or declarations signed ({count}). Any of them may have accepted it — the declaration says “I agree with the event's terms, conditions and rules” — and neither records which version of the terms it was, so nobody can be shown not to have relied on it, and deletion destroys the words themselves.
erase.termsWithdrawInstead: Withdrawal is what can be done: the version stays on the record, with its number, and is offered to nobody.
erase.termsAlreadyWithdrawn: You have already withdrawn it, so it is offered to nobody; it stays on the record, with its number, for whoever accepted it.

neonLimits.title: The database's limits
neonLimits.intro: Two brakes on the Neon bill, set in Neon itself: how large the database may grow, and how many CU-hours it may spend in a billing period. Everything here is read from Neon each time the page opens; after a save you see what Neon says, not what was sent.
neonLimits.unconfigured: {missing} is missing on this environment, so the page can neither read the limits nor change them. Set NEON_API_KEY and NEON_PROJECT_ID on the environment's Vercel project (SETUP.md §33) and redeploy.

failure.forbidden: Neon refused the key (HTTP {status}): the key in NEON_API_KEY may not read this project. The limits cannot be read, so they cannot be changed either.
failure.busy: Neon is working on another change to this project. Reload the page in a minute.
failure.refused: Neon refused the request (HTTP {status}). Check NEON_PROJECT_ID: it must be this environment's project.
failure.unavailable: Neon has a problem (HTTP {status}). The limits cannot be read now; reload the page later.
failure.timeout: Neon did not answer within 5 seconds. The limits cannot be read now, so they cannot be changed either; reload the page in a minute.
failure.network: Neon could not be reached (a network error). Reload the page in a minute.
failure.unexpected: Neon answered with something the page cannot read. The limits cannot be shown here; check them in the Neon console.

neonLimits.keyNeeded: The same key changes them when it may modify the project. A project-scoped key always may — Neon gives it Editor access to its one project (the organization's Settings → API keys → Create new → Project-scoped, on this environment's project) — and so does the personal key of an organization Admin or of an Editor on the project. The personal key of a Viewer reads the figures and cannot change them.
neonLimits.price: At Launch's rate ({rate} $/CU-hour), at the maximum size: at most {perHour} $ for each hour awake, which is {perMonth} $ a month if it stayed awake at the maximum all the time. The usual bill is the time awake: on average the database uses ≈ 0.25 CU.
neonLimits.usage: This period: {used} CU-hours spent, {active} hours awake; the period ends on {end}.
neonLimits.defaults: A compute created again gets {min}–{max} CU by default (the project's setting).
neonLimits.defaultsUnset: The project has no default size for a new compute; saving gives it the one chosen below.
neonLimits.manyComputes: The project has {count} read-write computes: the largest size is shown, and saving changes them all.
neonLimits.quotaActive: Limit in force: {hours} CU-hours, of which {used} spent. When it is reached, Neon stops the database until {end}.
neonLimits.readOnly: The Administrator changes the limits. The figures above are current for you too.
neonLimits.maxCuHelp: The site uses ≈ 0.25 CU on average; more only helps under heavy load. The minimum stays {min} CU. Beside each size, the worst case at Launch's rate: one hour awake at that size, and a whole month awake.
neonLimits.planCeiling: The account's plan allows at most {max} CU, so the larger sizes are not offered.
neonLimits.warningTitle: A monthly limit switches the site off
neonLimits.warning: When the limit is reached, Neon SUSPENDS the database until the next billing period ({end}), and it does not wake at the next connection. Until then the site does not work: no registrations, no race-day desk, no emails. This page needs the database too, so a limit that has stopped it can only be lifted in the Neon console.
neonLimits.recommend: Recommended: a monthly limit with room — {hours} CU-hours on this environment (SETUP.md §40; production spent about 4 CU-hours a day even on days of heavy testing) — together with the spending notification on Neon's Billing page as the early warning.
neonLimits.recommendConfirm: On production, a new, changed or removed limit needs the confirmation box below ticked: reached, the limit stops the site; removed, production is left with no cap.
neonLimits.quotaModeLimit: With a limit — the number below
neonLimits.quotaCuHours: CU-hours per period, with a limit

tasks.howTitle: How to do it, step by step

approveLegalText.title: Approve the legal text
approveLegalText.todo: A SAMPLE, unapproved text is on the site today. Until the club approves the privacy notice, the terms and the declaration, registration refuses everyone. The procedure is docs/RUNBOOKS.md § Legal document version.
approveLegalText.done: The club’s approved wording is published.
how: The short way (§132): /admin/legal → the “One step” box → check the legal name, CIF, seat and email shown → “Approve the three texts now”. Done: the notice, the terms and the declaration are in force, with the club's facts written in.
To read first: under the box, “start from the platform's text” → open each, read, then press the button in the box.
The long way, for a change: “New version” → text → save the draft → PDF → “Approve”. An approved text never changes; a correction is the next version.
On each event, under Registration, pick the approved declaration (if not already).

liveEmail.title: Email to real participants
liveEmail.todo: The sending domain {mailDomain} verified in Mailgun, then EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE=live on production — the steps are below. Until then messages are either captured or reach at most 5 authorised addresses in the sandbox (allowlist). Mode right now
how: In Mailgun: Sending → Domains → “Add new domain”. Name: {mailDomain}. Region: EU. Not the main domain — that stays free for the club's own mailboxes.

Mailgun shows the DNS records to create: two TXT (SPF and DKIM) and one CNAME (tracking). Add them at ROMARG → cPanel → Zone Editor exactly as Mailgun shows them, with the short name (no repeated domain). Mind the DKIM one: the value is over 255 characters and cPanel cuts it — enter it as two quoted strings on one line (“k=rsa; p=…first part” “…the rest”), or Mailgun sees it truncated. Then “Verify” in Mailgun — up to an hour.

Still in Mailgun: Sending → API keys → a sending key (MAILGUN_API_KEY). Sending → Webhooks → copy the “HTTP webhook signing key” (MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY) and add the webhook {webhookUrl} for “Permanent Failure” and “Spam Complaints” — the two the application acts on (a rejected address shows at the desk and on the registration). “Delivered” is optional.

In Vercel, the production project → Settings → Environment Variables (or `vercel env add NAME production`): MAILGUN_DOMAIN={mailDomain}, MAILGUN_API_KEY, MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY, MAILGUN_API_BASE_URL=https://api.eu.mailgun.net/v3, EMAIL_REPLY_TO=a mailbox the club reads (if none exists yet, leave the variable unset — an empty one is refused at startup). The sender is “{senderName}” <noreply@{mailDomain}> with no further setting — the name in EMAIL_FROM_NAME, the club’s own name by default.

Rehearse on QA, not on production (production refuses registrations until the legal texts are approved): on the QA Vercel project set the same MAILGUN_DOMAIN, MAILGUN_API_KEY, MAILGUN_API_BASE_URL (the mode stays allowlist, EMAIL_ALLOWLIST=your address), redeploy, register on QA — the email comes from noreply@{mailDomain}. When it does: on production EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE=live, redeploy. This row turns green.

scheduler.title: Production monitors on cron-job.org
scheduler.todo: Monitors for the two scheduled jobs (email-outbox and registration-maintenance), with this environment’s JOB_SECRET — SETUP.md §26: every 15 minutes by day (07–23, Romania time) and hourly at night. Email goes out right after each registration anyway; the monitors expire held places and retry what failed. Missing or late
scheduler.done: Both jobs are running on time.
how: On cron-job.org (free account): Settings → Time zone = Europe/Bucharest. Then “Create cronjob”, four times for production: two per address (one for the day, one for the night).

The addresses: {outboxUrl} and {maintenanceUrl}. On all of them: Request method POST, and under Headers: Authorization = Bearer followed by this environment's JOB_SECRET (the value in Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables; it is not shown here).

Day: Execution schedule → Custom → every day, hours 7–22, minutes 0, 15, 30, 45 (crontab */15 7-22 * * *). Night: Custom → every day, hours 23 and 0–6, minute 0 (0 0-6,23 * * *); the maintenance night job may skip 02:00 and 03:00 (0 0-1,4-6,23 * * *). A ping with nothing due answers without waking the database, so frequent pings cost nothing — the database wakes only when a job has work.

Turn on email notification on failure, so a dead monitor tells you. This row turns green on the first run; /devs shows each job with its last run, and the database's consumption. At night the site answers its first request more slowly — that is intended.

On QA: the outbox every hour (0 * * * *) and maintenance every 2 hours (0 */2 * * *), and on this page → Costuri „Cât de des verifică platforma” = 2 hours: QA pays for its own database's awake hours too.

The third monitor, the one that tells you when emails stop going out: “Create cronjob” with the address {baseUrl}/api/health, Request method GET, no header — production once an hour at minute 2 (Custom → every day, every hour, minute 2; leaving out 02:00 and 03:00 is fine: 2 0-1,4-23 * * *), QA every 6 hours (2 */6 * * *). Not every 30 minutes: each check wakes the database for five minutes, and that is what Neon bills. Under Notifications tick “on failure” (and “when the job gets disabled”). The page answers 503 while a message is deferred by the daily allowance, has failed, or was left unpicked by the monitors — and cron-job.org emails you from its own mail, not through Mailgun. When it clears, it answers 200 again and you get “job successful”.

inviteStaff.todo: There is a single staff account — the one inserted by hand. From /admin/staff an Administrator invites organizers by email address; their Zitadel account is bound on first sign-in.
how: Open /admin/staff, type the person's email address and pick the role: Moderator (writes and publishes), Administrator (registrations, legal texts, this page) or Superadministrator (the team too).

“Add” emails them the club's invitation: who added them, as what, the sign-in link. They open {baseUrl}/admin, sign in through Zitadel, done. “Access Denied” means an unverified email or a different address from the invited one.

inviteKey.title: The invitation key (Zitadel)
inviteKey.todo: The key is missing (ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT). Without it, “Add” on Echipa puts the person on the list and sends our invitation, but creates no sign-in account — and the sign-in page has no “create an account”, so the person is stuck. The key is a Zitadel service user's token with the Org User Manager role, set on both Vercel projects (SETUP.md §37).
inviteKey.blind: The key is set and authenticates, but can do nothing: asked which accounts it sees, Zitadel shows it not even yours — though you are signed in with it right now. The service user is not an “Org User Manager” of the organization. Every “Add” on Echipa writes the row and creates no account, and the colleague meets “User not found in the system” at sign-in (DECISIONS.md §288).
inviteKey.refused: The key is set, but Zitadel refuses the account search every “Add” makes — usually the token was revoked, or the service user is not an “Org User Manager” of the organization. Zitadel's answer
inviteKey.unreachable: The key could not be checked: Zitadel did not answer. Not necessarily a problem with the key — reload the page in a few minutes. The answer
inviteKey.done: The key works: checked just now with a real search, it found your account. “Add” on Echipa creates the sign-in account and Zitadel sends the password link.
how: Zitadel console → Users → Service Accounts → New: user name “brasovrunners-invites”, name “{club} — invitații”, access token type Bearer. Create.

Organization → Managers → + New: the service account, role Org User Manager (it may create users and send their invitation codes; nothing else). The dialog is called “Add an Administrator” and names the service user at the top; if it asks for a Loginname, that is “brasovrunners-invites”. Careful: “Role Assignments” is NOT this — that page grants roles inside a project and has nothing to do with managing users; a service account can sit there Active, looking configured, and still be unable to create anybody (DECISIONS.md §288).

On the service account → Personal Access Tokens → New. The console offers no expiry here and the token does not expire — it is a secret that has to be revoked by hand, on the same screen, when it is no longer wanted. Copy it (shown once) into the password manager and note there that it has no end date.
Vercel → the production project → Settings → Environment Variables: ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT = the token (Production). The same on the QA project. Redeploy both.

Check: reload this page after the redeploy — the row turns green when the key finds your account, without inviting anybody. Then, on Echipa, “Add” creates the account and Zitadel sends the password link; whoever has not signed in yet has “Resend the invitation” on their row.
howBroken: Zitadel console → Organization → Managers → + New: pick the key's service account (SETUP.md §37: “brasovrunners-invites”), role Org User Manager — it may create users and send their invitation codes, nothing else. The dialog is called “Add an Administrator”; if it asks for a Loginname, that is the service account's name.

Not “Role Assignments”: that page grants roles inside a project and has nothing to do with managing users. A service account can sit there Active, looking perfectly configured, and still be unable to create anybody — exactly what happened on the club's own instance (DECISIONS.md §288).

If Zitadel answered 401 or the token was revoked: on the service account → Personal Access Tokens → New, then the new token as ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT on both Vercel projects and redeploy (SETUP.md §37, steps 3–4).

Check: reload this page. The row turns green when the key finds your account — without inviting anybody. Then Echipa: every colleague marked “No sign-in account” was added while the key could not create accounts — ⋮ → “Revoke access”, then “Add” again with the same address; this time the account is created and Zitadel sends them the password link.
howUnreachable: Reload the page in a few minutes: the check runs on every open, with a single request to Zitadel.

If it stays so, open the Zitadel console: if that does not open either, the provider has a problem and there is nothing to do here; if it does, check on the service account that the token exists and, on Vercel, that ZITADEL_MANAGEMENT_PAT and AUTH_ZITADEL_ISSUER are set on this project (SETUP.md §37).

neonLimits.title: The database's monthly compute-time limit
neonLimits.todo: No monthly limit is set on this environment (or it could not be read from Neon — the card says which), so nothing caps the Neon bill. freeVerdict.freeExceptDomain: Yes, apart from the domain: every service is on a free plan and nothing is paid monthly.

mailgun.name: Mailgun (sending email)
mailgun.freeGives: Free: 100 emails a day — on one Mailgun account, used by both QA and production: what one sends comes off what the other can still send. Until the club has its own address, email can only go to five test addresses.
mailgun.ceiling: The first limit: 100 emails a day, which is about 33 entries, because one complete entry takes three emails.
mailgun.whenCrossed: Emails over the limit are not lost: they wait in the queue and go out after midnight. But a race whose confirmations only arrive the next morning is a bad race, so the paid plan is bought before entries open, not during them.

mailgun.bumpBack: Taken for the month of the race and stopped the month after. One month per race, not a long-term subscription.
mailgun.closeMeasuredMonth: This month {used} of {of} emails went out (plan {plan}) — enough for about {left} more registrations. Counted from this environment's own messages; the allowance belongs to one Mailgun account, shared with the other environment.

vercel.name: Vercel (where the site lives)
vercel.freeGives: Free: enough traffic and power for a club site, but only for non-commercial use.
vercel.ceiling: The first limit: the free plan requires that the site is not used commercially. The club sells nothing and takes no money, so we are fine.
vercel.whenCrossed: An event asking for a compulsory fee would count as commercial; a donation would not — they say so themselves. There is one more thing, and it has nothing to do with the club: if anybody is ever paid to work on this site, that counts as commercial too. And one more to know: if a limit on the free plan is exceeded, the feature stops for 30 days and you cannot pay to restart it — which is why you move up before a race, not during one.
vercel.closeYes: A published event is marked as charging a fee — check how it is worded.
vercel.closeNo: No published event asks for money.
vercel.bumpBack: This one does not come back down: it is not a busy weekend, it is a change in how the site is used. Unless it was taken purely for traffic.

neon.name: Neon (the database)
neon.freeGives: Free: a small database (half a gigabyte) and an amount of work included every month.
neon.ceiling: The first limit: the space and the monthly amount of work included.
neon.whenCrossed: On the free plan the database goes to sleep when nobody is using it, so the first page after a quiet spell is slow to load. Past the limit the site gets slow and errors can appear. The next step up is paid by usage, not as a fixed subscription.
neon.closeMeasured: Measured from the database: {used} MB of {of} MB used. Compute hours (CU) are on /devs.
neon.monthly: Monthly cost if we left Free, at this month's pace ({cu} CU-hours so far): about ${usd}/month on Launch (${rate}/CU-hour, ${storageRate}/GB, no subscription).
neon.monthlyUnknown: Monthly cost on Launch: ${rate}/CU-hour + ${storageRate}/GB, no subscription. The exact pace appears once NEON_API_KEY is set.
neon.closeUnknown: Not measured: the site does not know how much has been used. It is visible in the Neon account and worth a look before a race.
neon.closeNo: No ceiling on Launch: what is used is what is paid.
neon.bumpBack: Taken for the days entries are open and dropped once they close.

launch.freeGives: Launch: paid by usage, no subscription — compute hours and storage are billed at the plan's rates. The Free plan remains the way back, at the December review.
launch.ceiling: No ceiling: nothing stops when usage grows — the bill grows.
launch.whenCrossed: What keeps the bill small is what kept Free alive: the database sleeps after five minutes without a request, and the monitors wake it every 15 minutes by day and once an hour at night. A monitor every 5 minutes would keep it awake around the clock and turn sleeping hours into paid ones.
launch.close: No ceiling. This month, at the pace so far ({cu} CU-hours, about {perDay} CU-hours a day): about ${usd} a month (${rate}/CU-hour, ${storageRate}/GB-month) — an estimate; the invoice is Neon's.
launch.closeUnknown: No ceiling. The month's pace appears once NEON_API_KEY is set; until then the figure is in the Neon console → Billing (${rate}/CU-hour, ${storageRate}/GB-month).
launch.bumpBack: The way back is the December 2026 review: after real invoices, the club may choose Free again — one choice under “The Neon plan” on this page, no deployment; check Free's limits at that time on both projects first.

zitadel.name: Zitadel (how the team signs in)
zitadel.freeGives: Free: up to 100 sign-ins a day and a single administrator of the Zitadel account. Signing in happens on the provider's address, not the club's — decided, not pending: a login address of our own would cost 100 USD a month.
zitadel.ceiling: The one limit that matters: a single administrator of the Zitadel account. If that person is unavailable, nobody can invite anybody.
zitadel.whenCrossed: It is not crossed — it is written down: who the administrator is and where the credentials are (docs/RUNBOOKS.md § Staff sign-in).
zitadel.closeNo: The team signs in on the provider's address, as decided.

scheduler.name: cron-job.org + GitHub (the automatic jobs)
scheduler.freeGives: Both free: cron-job.org calls the two jobs every 15 minutes (email goes out right after each registration regardless), and GitHub Actions is the safety net when the first does not.
scheduler.ceiling: Here the limit is not money but rhythm: without the cron-job.org monitors the jobs only run from the safety net, roughly every two hours.
scheduler.whenCrossed: Email waits in the queue, and places held for somebody are released later than they should be. Nothing breaks and nobody loses their place — but the confirmation arrives late, and on registration day that feels like a broken site.

jobCadence.title: How often the platform checks
jobCadence.intro: The platform has two scheduled jobs: registration maintenance (holds that lapse, waiting-list offers, reminders, race numbers) and the email outbox. An external service calls them every 15 minutes by day and hourly at night. When they have nothing to do they answer from Vercel's cache without waking the database — and Neon bills every wake-up as at least 5 minutes of compute. Here you choose how often, at most, they may look at the database.

jobCadence.onTheHour: The safety check happens on the hour (with 2 hours, on the even hours), together with the /api/health monitor, so an idle hour costs at most one wake of the database rather than one per job. With an interval chosen, the checks also keep to its marks on the clock (:00 and :30, the hour, the even hours); getting there may make some checks up to a quarter of an hour late each.

desk.title: Number pickup desk
desk.howTitle: How race day works, step by step
how: Before the race (organizer): on the event page, under “Taking part and registration” → “Allocate and print”, press “Download every number (PDF)” and print them — two to an A4 sheet. Print a few “Paper declaration form (PDF)” too, for anyone who signs on the spot.

Volunteers: a Superadministrator makes their accounts from “Staff”, with the Volunteer role. With their account they open this page on their phone. That is all they see: name, state, number. No email addresses, and nobody can be cancelled from here.

Every confirmed participant got a QR code by email. At the desk: press “Scan” (on Android) or open the phone's camera and point it at the code — the person's row opens. Or search by name or by race number.
Press “Mark present” and hand over the number from the pile. No number? Type it in the box and press “Save no.”.

No email arrived, or they cannot find the QR: search by name. If it says “Așteaptă semnarea declarației” (awaiting the declaration), give them the paper declaration to sign, press “Confirm on paper”, then “Mark present”.

Never registered at all: “Add somebody” — name and email; the “This person is at the desk” tick is already set. They sign the paper declaration, then “Mark present”. If the event is full they join the waiting list; “Give a place” only works once one is free.
Made a mistake? “Undo” takes it back. Every press stays in the registration's history, with your name on it.
At the end, the figures on this page are the race's figures: how many confirmed, how many here. Whoever did not come stays without “here”.

A red box saying “Registration cancelled” or “expired”? The person no longer has a place, even with the email in hand: no number, no check-in. If it says the number was printed, pull that bib out of the pile — numbers are never reused.

when.DECLARATION_SIGNED: Not sent any more: the signed declaration, as a PDF, goes attached to “Registration confirmed”, together with a link to it.
when.DECLARATION_ARCHIVE: Together with the signed declaration, to the club's declarations mailbox set above (or DECLARATIONS_ARCHIVE_TO, when none is set here) — only for real registrations. No action link; in the attached PDF the identity document's series and number are masked.
when.BIB_ASSIGNED: Automatically, once, when registration closes and the numbers become final; and when an organizer types or changes the number of a confirmed registration, from its page or at the desk. With the QR code and the manage link. Never for a cancelled event.
when.STAFF_INVITATION: When an administrator adds somebody on Echipa, and on "Resend the invitation" while that person has not signed in yet. To the colleague's address, no token: the sign-in page decides who they are.
when.REGISTRATION_OPENED: Automatically, on the maintenance job's first run after registration opens (within a quarter of an hour by day, an hour at night), to every address left at "Tell me" on the event's page while registration was still ahead. One message; the address is deleted from the notification list with it. No token — the button leads to the ordinary registration form.
when.CLUB_CONFIRMATION_NOTICE: On every confirmation of a real registration, to the club addresses above. No action link and no token.
when.EVENT_UPDATE_NOTICE: Only when an organizer ticks “Tell participants about the change” while saving the event, and only if the place, the date and time or the programme changed, or they wrote a note. One email to every active registration (waiting for the declaration, on the waiting list, offered a place, confirmed), in its language; the place and time are the ones at sending time. No token: the button leads to the event's page. Unticked, nothing is sent.
when.EVENT_CANCELLED: When an organizer sets the event's status to “Cancelled” and leaves “Tell the participants” ticked. With the reason they wrote, to every active registration, in its language. The registrations are not cancelled; no token and no action link.
when.ORGANIZER_MESSAGE: Only when an organizer writes and sends a message from the event's page → “Send a message to participants” — bad weather or a last-minute change, for instance. The subject and the text are written for each send, in Romanian and English; the preview here uses a sample text. To the group chosen — confirmed, on the waiting list, with the declaration unsigned, or all — each in their own language. No token and no attachment: the button leads to the event's page.
when.GROUP_RUN_DECLARATION_SIGNED: Right after somebody signs the optional declaration on a group run's page, to the address they gave. With the declaration as a PDF, whole; no token and no action link — there is no registration to manage.
when.GROUP_RUN_DECLARATION_ARCHIVE: Together with a declaration signed on a group run, to the club's declarations mailbox set above (or DECLARATIONS_ARCHIVE_TO, if none is set here). No action link; in the attached PDF the identity document's series and number are masked.
when.REGISTER_ANOTHER_PERSON: When the public form is sent again with an address already registered for the event and another name. No registration is created, and the screen shows the same “check your email” as always. The address gets a single-use link, valid for {confirmation}, to the form with the address fixed — or, if it already has {people}, only the sentence that says so, with no link.
when.NEWSLETTER_CONFIRM: As soon as someone subscribes in the contact page's pop-up: the link that confirms the subscription, valid for {confirmation}. An address already subscribed gets, instead, the link to its own subscription, and nothing changes. An unconfirmed address receives nothing else.
when.NEWSLETTER: Only when an organizer writes and sends a newsletter from the backoffice's “Newsletter” page. To the subscribers of the topic chosen and those who receive everything, each in their own language first, with the unsubscribe link. It leaves after every other email, and only from the part of the allowance left above the reserve kept for registrations.
when.NEW_EVENT_ALERT: Automatically, once for each new event published (never the weekly run), on the job's first run after publication: to those subscribed to new events and to the event's own topics (a race, a special event, gear testing) and those who receive everything, with the unsubscribe link.
