guide.title: How to use the platform
guide.intro: Every task has its own numbered steps. What is written «like this», in bold, is exactly what the button or the screen says — look for those words. Your role's sections come first and open; press a task to see its steps. If a button is missing, you do not have the role for it: ask a superadministrator for it, or ask someone who has that role.

sections.title: First steps
sections.who: For everyone: sign in, find your way, confirm what you press.

tasks.title: Sign in to the backoffice
steps: The first time: open the invitation email the club sent you and choose your password from it.
Open the club's site and add /en/admin at the end of the address.
On the «Staff sign-in» page press «Sign in» and use the email address the invitation came to and your password.
The top says «Signed in as» with your name and role. If the role is not the one you expected, tell a superadministrator.
On a computer that is not yours, press «Sign out» when you finish.

tasks.title: The top bar: what each tab holds
steps: You see only your role's tabs; the rest do not exist for you, and that is fine.
«Events»: every club event; «New event» and «Edit» are here.
«Race day»: the number pickup desk, on a phone.
«Registrations»: who signed up, with filters, the export and each registration's page.
«Legal documents»: the terms, the privacy notice (GDPR) and the declarations.
«Emails»: what participants receive, the Mailgun plan and «Deadlines».

«Tasks» → «Club»: what the club still has to do, read from the system, with the steps under each row. «Tasks» → «To do»: the club's list, typed and ticked by hand — add a line, give it to somebody, set a due day, tick it when it is done.
«Pages», «Gallery», «Staff», «Configuration» and «Guide» (this page).

tasks.title: The question before an important press
steps: Whatever publishes, cancels, erases or sends emails asks first, in a window. Read it: it says what happens and how many participants get an email.
To go ahead, press the button with the same name in the window. To stop, «Never mind».
Once it worked, a message at the bottom says for a few seconds what was done.
If something is missing, a red box at the top names each gap as a link: tap it, fill it in, press again. What you typed stays.

tasks.title: What each role can do
steps: The Volunteer: the race-day desk — finds a runner, confirms on the paper declaration the participant signed, gives a free place, a number, checks people in. Sees a name, a state and a number, never an email address.
The Redactor: the events' texts and the site's pages, in both languages. Does not change an event's settings and does not publish.

The Organizer: reads every registration, the export and the race numbers; changes the event's settings (date, place, route, cost, registration); messages participants. Does not write the texts, publish, cancel or erase a registration, resend emails or assign numbers.
The Tehnic role: the platform's configuration page, for troubleshooting; may correct an event's settings. Does not see the registrations.

The Administrator: everything the Organizer and the Redactor do, plus «Create and publish», correcting, cancelling and erasing a registration, resending emails, «Assign numbers», «Deadlines» and the Mailgun plan. Reads the legal documents but does not write or approve them, and does not see «Staff».

The Superadministrator: everything the Administrator does, plus the legal documents (new version, approval, withdrawal, deletion) and the accounts under «Staff» (add, change role, revoke access). A task in this guide that needs this role starts with “Role needed: Superadministrator”; if you do not have it, ask a Superadministrator to do it or to give it to you.

tasks.title: What cannot be done
steps: Nobody changes a participant's confirmed email address, not even an Administrator.
Nobody merges two registrations into one.
Nobody on the team signs the declaration for the participant: at the desk you only record the paper declaration they signed themselves.
No legal text takes effect without an approved version; without approved terms, notice and declaration nobody can register.
Nobody goes past the number of places: there is no registration over capacity, not by hand and not at the desk. A place is given only when it is free.

sections.title: Race day — the number pickup desk
sections.who: Volunteer, Organizer and every other role. On a phone.

tasks.title: Open the desk
steps: Sign in (see “First steps”). A Volunteer lands on the desk; everyone else presses «Race day» in the top bar.
Under «Event» pick today's race, then press «Search».
At the top you see how many are confirmed, how many are here, how many have no number and how many are unconfirmed. Those are the race's figures.

tasks.title: A participant with the QR code
steps: The participant shows you the QR code from the confirmation email.
Press «Scan» and hold the code in the frame (it works on Android). On an iPhone: open the Camera app, point it at the code and tap the link that appears.
The person's row opens: check the name with them.
Press «Mark present». It asks nothing; a message appears at the bottom.
Hand over the race number from the pile — the number is shown large on the row. To see the number drawn: «Show the race number (BID)».
For the next one: «Back to the desk».

tasks.title: No QR: search by name
steps: In the «Name, number or code» box type part of the name, the race number or the code from the email.
Press «Search».
On the right row: «Mark present», then hand over the number.

tasks.title: They have not signed the declaration
steps: The row says «Așteaptă semnarea declarației» (awaiting the declaration) or «Așteaptă confirmarea emailului» (awaiting the email confirmation).
Give them the printed declaration form. They read it and sign it themselves. A minor: the parent or guardian signs too, each with their own document.
Press «Confirm on paper», then «Confirm on paper» again in the window.
Then «Mark present» and the number. Keep the signed sheet for the organizer.

tasks.title: No race number
steps: In the «Race number (BIB)» box on their row type a free number.
Press «Save no.» and confirm in the window. A number somebody else already has is refused — pick another.

tasks.title: Never registered
steps: Press «Add somebody».
Fill in the first name, the last name, the birth date, the phone and «Participant email address».
The «This person is at the desk…» tick is already set — leave it.
Tick «I confirm this person asked me to register them…».
Press «Add the registration» and confirm in the window.
Give them the paper declaration to sign, then «Mark present» and the number.
Event full? They join the waiting list, like anyone. «Give a place» works only once a place has freed up.

tasks.title: Pressed the wrong thing
steps: On the same row press «Undo».
Everything you press stays in the registration's history, with your name. Nothing is lost.

tasks.title: A red box: cancelled or expired registration
steps: The person no longer has a place, even with the email in hand: give no number and do not mark them present.
If it says the number was printed, pull that bib from the pile — numbers are never reused.
Call an organizer. If places are left, you register them again with «Add somebody».

tasks.title: What you do not do at the desk (and that is fine)
steps: You see no email addresses, and you do not cancel, erase or export lists. For those, call an Administrator.

sections.title: Copywriter — the events' texts and the pages
sections.who: Role: Copywriter (Redactor). You write; you do not configure or publish.

tasks.title: Correct an event's text
steps: «Events» → «Edit» on the event's row.
Open the card with the text: «Title and summary», «Event description», «The day's programme and what to bring» or «Rules».
Write in the «Română» tab and in the «English» tab.
At the bottom, on a published event, tick «I understand that I am editing published content.».
Press «Save». It is on the site at once, in both languages.

tasks.title: Put a picture in the text
steps: In the text editor put the cursor where the picture goes.
Press «Picture» in the editor's toolbar.
Under «Quality» leave «Medium (recommended)».
Press «Choose the picture» and pick the file. A picture already uploaded comes from «From gallery».
Write «What the picture shows (alt text)», then «Done».
Press «Save».

tasks.title: Add a YouTube film
steps: In the editor press «YouTube».
Paste the address into «The film's address (YouTube)» and press «Add the film».
Press the film to write its «Caption (under the film)».
Press «Save». On the page the film loads only when the reader presses it.

tasks.title: Write a page of the site
steps: «Pages» → «New page».
Write the title and the text in Romanian and in English, then press «New page».
On its page, after every change, «Save».
When it is ready, «Trimite spre verificare» (submit for review). The Administrator publishes it.

tasks.title: The two-languages rule
steps: An event is not published without a title and a summary in Romanian and in English.

An optional text (the description, the rules, the programme's notes, the SEO fields) is written in both languages or neither: the save refuses one language only and points at the empty box, with everything you typed kept.
If the English text is identical to the Romanian one, the editor asks whether it is translated — a warning only.

tasks.title: What is not yours
steps: The event's settings (date, place, places, registration), publishing, the gallery and the registrations. If a text depends on a wrong setting, tell the Organizer or the Administrator.

sections.title: Organizer — registrations, numbers, messages
sections.who: Role: Organizer (Organizator). You see everything and change the event's settings; you do not publish, cancel or erase registrations.

tasks.title: See who registered
steps: Press «Registrations» in the top bar.
Under «Events» pick the event (or «All events»), under «Status» what you need, then «Filter».
Looking for someone: type part of the name in «Search by name» and press «Filter». With no event chosen, it looks in every event.
The «How far» column says each person's step. Press a name to open the registration: «The registration's journey» and «Timeline» say everything that happened.
The top says once what you cannot change here. The Tehnic role does not see registrations at all.

tasks.title: Download the list (Excel or CSV)
steps: «Registrations» → pick the event → «Filter».
Press «Export to Excel» (or «Export CSV»). The file holds exactly the filtered rows, without test registrations.
The file carries identity documents and phone numbers: never send it to a group, and delete it within 7 days of the event.

tasks.title: Add a registration for someone who asked
steps: «Registrations» → «Add a registration».
Under «Event» pick the event.
Fill in the person's details, «Participant email address» and «Language we write to them in».
Tick «I confirm this person asked me to register them…».
The person is not in front of you? Leave «This person is at the desk…» unticked: they get the email and sign their own declaration.
Press «Add the registration» and confirm in the window.
Refused because the address already has a registration: the family's second person registers from the public form (see “A family on one address”).

tasks.title: Download and print the race numbers
steps: «Events» → «Edit» on the race.
Open the «Taking part and registration» card, then «Allocate and print».
«See the bibs» to check them on screen.
«Download every number (PDF)»: two A5 numbers on each A4 sheet, with the cut line. «One per page» for a single one, centred on A4.
Print at actual size (100%) and cut on the line.
Numbers go in registration order, from «Race numbers (BIB) start at». «Assign numbers» is the Administrator's.

tasks.title: A chosen number for someone
steps: «Registrations» → open the person's registration.
Press «Change the number»; the free numbers are listed under the box. No such button? The number is already final and is not changed from here.
Type the number, press «Save no.» and confirm. The person gets the number by email. A number somebody else already wears is refused.

tasks.title: Send a message to the participants
steps: «Events» → «Edit» → the «Registrations received» card → «Send a message to participants».
Under «Who receives it» pick the group (everyone, «Only the confirmed», the waiting list or those without a declaration) and see how many they are.
Write the «Subject» and the «Message», in Romanian and in English.
Under «How the email looks» read both versions: «Registered in Romanian» and «Registered in English».
Press «Send the message», then «Send» in the window. The message stays under «Messages sent».
About this event only: no advertising, no sponsors' offers, no other events.

tasks.title: Write to the newsletter subscribers
steps: Press «Newsletter» in the top bar. See how many confirmed subscribers there are, per topic, and what was sent; no address appears, only the numbers.
Under «Write to the subscribers» pick the topic under «What it is about» and see how many receive it.
Write «Subject (Romanian)», «Subject (English)», «Text (Romanian)» and «Text (English)».
Under «How it looks» read the email in both languages.
Press «Send the newsletter» and confirm. The message stays under «Sent». The new-event announcements go by themselves.

tasks.title: Get race day ready
steps: Print the numbers (see above).
«Events» → «Edit» → «Registrations received»: print a few «Paper declaration form (PDF)» and, if it is there, «Paper declaration form for a minor (PDF)».
There too, «Emergency sheet»: the phones and emergency contacts of everyone confirmed, on one page. Take it to the race and destroy it afterwards.
Volunteers: ask a superadministrator to make their accounts with the Voluntar role, then show them this guide's “Race day” section.
On race day: «Race day» in the top bar.

tasks.title: Change a setting of the event
steps: «Events» → «Edit».
Open the card: «Date and time», «The place», «The course», «Cost» or «Taking part and registration». Change what is needed.
At the bottom, in the «Save» card, on a published event tick «I understand that I am editing published content.».
Must the participants know? Tick «Tell participants about the change» and write the note in both languages.
Press «Save». The texts (the title, the description) are not yours to save: tell the Administrator what is wrong.

tasks.title: The signed declarations
steps: All of an event's: «Events» → «Edit» → «Registrations received» → «Signed declarations (PDF)».
One person's: open the registration → «Signed declaration (PDF)».
They carry identity documents: keep them only in the club's archive.

tasks.title: What the Administrator does, not you
steps: Creating and publishing events, cancelling or erasing registrations, resending emails, «Assign numbers», marking numbers printed and sending the thank-you. Tell them what needs doing.

tasks.title: Create an event
steps: «Events» → «New event».
Each card is a part of the public page, in the site's order. The map at the top, «The page, top to bottom», takes you to each card.
«What kind of event» → «Event type» (Race, Group run and the others).
«Title and summary»: «Title» and «Summary», in the «Română» tab and in the «English» tab.
«Date and time», then «The place»: the meeting point in both languages, the address, the map link. Place not known yet? Tick «Location to be announced».
The other cards as needed: «Event description», «The course», «Cost», «Taking part and registration», «The day's programme and what to bring», «Rules».
«Create the event» saves it as a draft (not on the site). «Create and publish» puts it on the site at once.
Something required missing? «Cannot publish yet» appears at the top, each gap a link: fill it in and press again.
The usual mistake: leaving the «English» tab empty leaves the event with no English half; or pressing «Create the event» thinking it went live — it stays a draft, unlike «Create and publish».

tasks.title: Edit an event
steps: «Events» → «Edit» on its row.
A closed card says on its line what is missing, per language. Open the card and change what is needed.
Write in «Română» and in «English»: an optional text is written in both languages or neither.
At the bottom, in the «Save» card, on a published event tick «I understand that I am editing published content.».
A date of a series: under «Save for:» pick «This date only», «This and the following dates» or «All dates of the series».
Press «Save». It is on the site at once, in both languages.
The usual mistake: picking «This date only» when you meant the whole series (or the other way round) — check the message under «Save for:» before you press «Save».

tasks.title: Put a picture in the summary or the description
steps: Open the card («Title and summary» or «Event description») and put the cursor where the picture goes.
Press «Picture» in the editor's toolbar.
Under «Quality» leave «Medium (recommended)».
Press «Choose the picture» and pick the file. A picture already uploaded comes from «From gallery».
Write «What the picture shows (alt text)», then «Done».
Press «Save». To replace a picture: press it, «Remove the picture», then put in the new one.

tasks.title: Publish an event, or take it off the site
steps: «Events» → «Edit» → the «Publication» card.
A draft: press «Trimite spre verificare» (submit for review), then «Publică» (publish).
In the window press «Publică» again. Both languages go live together.
Something missing? «Cannot publish yet» appears with the list: fill it in, «Save», then «Publică».
Several at once: on the «Events» list tick them and press «Publish the ticked ones».
To take it off the site: «Mută în ciornă» (back to draft). Once it has happened: «Arhivează» (archive).

tasks.title: Repeat an event (a weekly series)
steps: «Events» → «Edit» → the «Recurrence» card.
Tick «Repeat this event», pick the days and until when.
Press «Create the dates» and confirm.

The platform creates the new dates by itself, {horizon} ahead. Those created as drafts show on the «Events» list with «Publish» on the row; «Publish automatically from now on» publishes them by themselves from now on.
A copy, not a series: on the list, «More actions» (⋮) → «Duplicate». The copy is a draft.

tasks.title: Open registration for a race
steps: «Events» → «Edit» → the «Taking part and registration» card.
«Registration mode» → «Înscrieri pe site» (registration on the site).
«Capacity» and «Maximum waiting-list length» (empty = no limit, 0 = no list).
«Registration period»: «Registration opens» and «Registration closes».
«Confirmation window»: «Participation confirmation: asked how many days before» and, in the box beside it, how many days before it is due (0 = the place never lapses before the start).
«Who may enter»: «Declaration a participant signs» and «Minimum age (years)» (14 unless you change it, 0 for none).
«Race numbers (bibs)»: «Race numbers (BIB) start at».
Press «Save», then publish the event. Nobody can register while the terms, the privacy notice and the declaration are not approved.

tasks.title: Tell the participants about a change
steps: Change the place, the time or the programme in their card.
In the «Save» card tick «Tell participants about the change».
Write «What changed (optional)» in Romanian and in English.
Press «Save». The window says how many get an email; press «Save» again.
The email goes only if the place, the start or the programme changed, or if you wrote a note.

tasks.title: Cancel an event
steps: «Events» → «Edit» → the «Event status» card (at the bottom, among the cards that are not on the page).
Under «Event status» pick «Anulat» (cancelled).
The «Save» card shows «You are cancelling the event»: write «Why the event is cancelled» in Romanian and in English.
Tick «Tell the participants that the event is cancelled». Without the tick no email goes out.
Press «Save». The red window says how many get an email; press «Save» again.

tasks.title: Correct, cancel or erase a registration
steps: «Registrations» → find the person → press their name.
Wrong name: under «Correct the name» type the right one → «Save the name».
Not coming any more: «Cancel the registration», write the «Reason», press «Cancel the registration» and confirm. The place goes to the waiting list.
The email never arrived: «Resend email».
They ask for their data to be erased: «Delete permanently», write the «Reason for deletion», tick «I confirm this deletion is permanent» and press «Delete permanently».
Several at once: tick the rows on the list → «Cancel the ticked ones».

tasks.title: Assign the numbers and mark them printed
steps: «Events» → «Edit» → «Taking part and registration» → «Allocate and print».
Press «Assign numbers» and confirm: every confirmed registration without a number gets the next free one; numbers already given stay.
«Registrations» → pick the race → «Filter». On the same page you download the unprinted numbers, print them, then press the button that marks them printed.
The numbers for printing are two A5 on each A4 sheet (see “Download and print the race numbers” under Organizer).

tasks.title: The Mailgun plan, before and after a race
steps: First pay for the plan in the Mailgun account.
«Emails» → «The Mailgun plan, and how much we can still send».
Under «The plan the Mailgun account is on» pick Basic; under «Note (why, until when)» write why and until when.
Press «Save the plan» and confirm. The figures on «Tasks» and the «Send now» button follow it.
After the race: cancel in Mailgun, then put Free back here and «Save the plan».

tasks.title: Remove an address from the newsletter
steps: When someone asks in writing to stop receiving the news: «Newsletter» → «Remove an address at someone's request».
Type the address under «Email address», press «Remove from the newsletter» and confirm. The address is deleted, with its topics.

tasks.title: The club's deadlines
steps: «Emails» → «Deadlines».
Change the numbers (the email link, the held place, the waiting-list offer, the reminder, check-in, the series).
Press «Save the deadlines» and confirm. Only what is given from now on takes the new deadlines.

tasks.title: The thank-you after a race
steps: «Events» → «Edit» → «Registrations received» → «Thank-you after the race».
Under «Link (optional)» put the address of the photos or the results.
Press «Send the thank-you» and confirm. It goes once, to everyone marked present.

tasks.title: Pages and the gallery
steps: A page: «Pages» → «New page» (or an existing one) → write in both languages → «Save». On the pages list, the ⋮ menu on its row → «Publish».
An album: «Gallery» → «New album» → the date, the event, the title in both languages → «New album».
On the album's page: «Upload photos», with «Quality» «Medium (recommended)»; pick a «Cover».
On the albums list, the ⋮ menu on its row → «Publish the album». An album with no photos is not published.

tasks.title: What the club still has to do
steps: «Tasks» → the «Club» tab: every row is read from the system, with the steps under it. A green row is done.
«Costs»: what the club pays and the database's limits.

tasks.title: Accounts for volunteers and colleagues (Superadministrator)
steps: Role needed: Superadministrator. «Staff» shows only for one; an Administrator does not see it and asks them.
«Staff» → «Add someone»: «Email address», «Name», «Role» (Voluntar for the desk), «Preferred language».
Press «Add» and confirm. The person gets the invitation by email and chooses a password.
It never arrived: on their row, «Resend the invitation».
Another role: «Change role». Left the team: «Revoke access».

sections.title: Legal documents and personal data (GDPR)
sections.who: Role: an Administrator reads; writing, approving, withdrawing and deleting the texts need a Superadministrator. Read once, before the first race with registrations.

tasks.title: Approve a new version of a legal text
steps: Role needed: Superadministrator. Only they see «New version» and approve; an Administrator reads the texts and the PDFs but does not write, approve or withdraw a version.
«Legal documents» → «New version».
Under «Start from the platform's text» pick the document: «Racing TOS», «GDPR», «Self-declaration (race)», «Self-declaration (group run, asphalt)» or «Self-declaration (group run, trail)».
The text comes with the club's details filled in. Whatever is left in angle brackets, shaped <…>, you fill in in Romanian and in English.
Read all of it and press «Save draft».
On the draft's page: «Download PDF» to read it on paper or give it to a lawyer.
Under «Approve this version» tick «I confirm the club has approved this text and it may become public», press «Approve and publish» and confirm.
An approved text never changes. A correction is the next version: «Start the next version from this one».

tasks.title: The five texts, before the race is published
steps: Role needed: Superadministrator. In one sitting, each from «Start from the platform's text»: the terms, the privacy notice (GDPR), the race declaration, the asphalt declaration, the trail declaration.
Without approved terms, notice and declaration nobody can register. Without the trail declaration approved, no trail run offers the declaration.
Until you approve the new notice, the public participant list shows the confirmed only.

tasks.title: How the declaration is signed
steps: The participant reads the text filled in with their name and the event, types their identity document's series and number (no ID picture is ever uploaded) and signs with a finger or the mouse.
A minor aged 14 or over signs with the parent's consent; under 14 only the parent or guardian signs — as the approved declaration says.
Kept: the names, the documents, the text's version, its fingerprint, the moment and the method. It is a simple electronic signature.
Right after, they get the signed declaration by email, as a PDF. At the desk, the kit is handed over against the document written in the declaration.
Whoever cannot sign online signs on paper at the desk, and the volunteer presses «Confirm on paper». The club keeps the signed original.

tasks.title: Minors and the minimum age
steps: A participant under 18 is registered by a parent or guardian, who writes their name in the form's section for minors; the desk and the export show “Minor — parent/guardian”.

The minimum age is each event's own: «Minimum age (years)», under «Taking part and registration». It is counted on the day of the event, at every door — the form, the desk, a registration entered by staff.

tasks.title: Where the data lives and how long it is kept
steps: Declarations are records in the database, not files; the PDF is made on request, identically.
Registrations and declarations are kept 3 years from the event, then deleted by themselves. The emergency contact and the health note are deleted 7 days after the event.
Downloaded exports and PDFs that carry identity documents are yours to delete, within 7 days of the event.
The privacy notice says exactly this.

tasks.title: A GDPR request: access, withdrawal, erasure
steps: «Registrations» → find the person → open the registration.
What we hold about them: «Everything held about this person».
Withdraw a consent (the health note, the socials, the public results): «Withdraw consent» → tick what they withdraw → «Reason» → «Withdraw».
Erasure: «Delete permanently» (see “Correct, cancel or erase a registration”). The history keeps who erased and why, never the person's data.

sections.title: The participant — their steps, and how to test them
sections.who: No account. Everything by email. Walk them once on the test site (QA), with your own address.

tasks.title: Registering, from the form to the QR code
steps: On the event page press «Register for this event».
Fill in the form. For a race: «Read the race conditions», scroll to the end, then «I have read them and I agree». Tick the terms too.
Press «Submit registration». If something is missing, «Still missing:» appears above the button with each item — tap one and it takes you there.
In the email press «Confirm your email». The link is valid for {confirmation}.
Sign the declaration: on the page that opens, or from the «Sign the declaration» email → «Sign and confirm».
They get the confirmation with the QR code and the race number, plus the signed declaration as a PDF.
Check in the backoffice: «Registrations» → search the name → the status «Confirmată» (confirmed).

tasks.title: Their place and deadlines
steps: Once the address is confirmed, the place is held for {hold} (or until the confirmation deadline, for an event further away than its window). The deadline matters only if somebody is waiting for a place; otherwise the place stays theirs until the start.
Event full: they join the waiting list. When a place frees up they get an email and have {offer} to sign the declaration.
From {checkin} before the start, from «Manage your registration» they can press «I have arrived — mark me as here». They still pick up the number at the desk.

tasks.title: They withdraw or cannot come any more
steps: From the confirmation email: «Manage your registration» → «Cancel registration».
From the reminder: «I can't come — cancel my registration».
Any time: «My registrations», on the site, with their address. The place goes to the waiting list at once.

tasks.title: No email arrived
steps: On the site, «Send the registration link again» → the address → «Send the link».
Or they come to the desk and a volunteer confirms them there, on paper.

tasks.title: Events in their calendar
steps: Every event has Google Calendar and the calendar file (.ics).
On the events page they can subscribe to the club's whole calendar; it updates by itself when you publish something new.

sections.title: A family on one address
sections.who: For every role. How several people register with the same email.

tasks.title: Register a second person on the same address
steps: The first person registers as usual.

The form is sent again with the same address for a different person — another name and another birth date than every person already registered. Nobody is registered yet: the screen shows the same “check your email” as always, so nobody learns from the form who is registered.
The address gets the email “Registering one more person?”, with who is already registered and the person from the form, and one button, «I confirm I am registering another person».

The page it opens shows the details again; for an adult it asks one tick (the person declares their own health when they sign). The confirmation registers them straight away — no second confirmation link. The link is valid for {confirmation} and works once; unconfirmed details are deleted by themselves after that.
If only the name or only the birth date differs, nobody is registered: the address gets the existing registration's email, with one sentence on how to register someone else.
One address may register at most {people} for an event. At the limit, the email says so and carries no button.

tasks.title: What follows for each person
steps: Each person signs their own declaration (their own email with the declaration) — an adult never signs for another adult; a minor signs as usual. Each has their own place, their own race number and, if it comes to it, their own place on the waiting list.
The address receives one QR code for each confirmed person, in separate emails.
At the desk you scan each code in turn: each opens that person's own row.

tasks.title: What you see in the backoffice
steps: In «Registrations», at the desk and in the export, each person is a row of their own, with the same address.
«My registrations» lists every registration of the address, each with its name. Cancelling or erasing one leaves the others alone.
Reminders and thank-yous come one per person.

tasks.title: Change the limit per address (Administrator)
steps: «Emails» → «Deadlines» → «Registrations per address (per event)».
Type the number, press «Save the limit» and confirm.

sections.title: When something goes wrong
sections.who: For everyone. What to check, and who to write to.

tasks.title: Check whether the platform is working
steps: Open /api/health in a new tab and read only the first word after "status", at the very start of the text: ok means the platform is working, degraded or down means a problem, even if ok appears further down.
Not sure what you see? Send the text to the club's owner.

tasks.title: Write to someone when something is wrong
steps: A page shows an error, a button does nothing, or a press never finishes? Take a screenshot of what it says.
Write to the club's owner or a superadministrator: what you pressed, on what page, and the screenshot.
Do not wait for it to fix itself: an email that never sent or a stuck registration matters to someone waiting.

tasks.title: A save fails from an office laptop
steps: An office network sometimes blocks the request to the server, especially a company one.
Try again after turning on your phone's hotspot and connecting the laptop to it.
Works over the hotspot but not the office network? Tell someone at the office — it is the network's problem, not the platform's.

guide.yours: Your role: {role}. Your sections come first and open; the rest are your colleagues'.
guide.familyPending: Not switched on yet: the database still keeps one registration per address per event, until BR-V1.94, the update that changes it. Until then, sending the form again for another person only re-sends the first registration's email.
guide.network: A save fails on an office laptop?

erase.title: Permanent deletion: {event}
erase.whatGoes: This permanently deletes the event “{event}” of {date}, in both languages, together with its {count} registrations and the personal data behind them.
erase.realPeople: {count} of the registrations belong to real people. They go with their signed declarations and their addresses, and nothing can be recovered.
erase.noRealPeople: No real registration: nobody loses a place.
erase.alternative: If the event took place, archive it instead: it stays in the records and disappears from the site. Permanent deletion is for an event that should never have existed.
erase.typeTitleHelp: Type “{title}” exactly, to confirm. Anything else stops the deletion.
erase.reasonHelp: It is kept in the audit trail. It is the only thing that survives the deletion; the names of the people erased are kept nowhere.
erase.action: Permanently delete the event and its registrations

forms.kept: What you typed is still in the boxes; correct it and send again.
forms.keptConflict: What you typed is still in the boxes — copy what you need, then reload the page.
forms.keptExceptConfirmation: What you typed is still in the boxes, except the confirmation, which is asked again.

participantMessages.title: Send a message to participants
participantMessages.intro: An email you write, in Romanian and English, to the people registered for this event — bad weather, a last-minute change or a cancellation, for instance. Each receives it in the language they registered in, with the other language below and with the link to the event's page. It goes through the email queue, like every other message.
participantMessages.audienceHelp: Cancelled or lapsed registrations and unconfirmed email addresses receive nothing. The number beside each group is the registrations as they are now.

audiences.ALL_ACTIVE: Everyone registered: confirmed, on the waiting list and those who have not signed the declaration yet
audiences.WAITLIST: Only the waiting list (and those offered a place)
audiences.PENDING_DECLARATION: Only those registered who have not signed the declaration yet

participantMessages.nobody: Nobody is in the chosen group right now.
participantMessages.nobodyYet: Nobody is registered for this event right now, so there is nobody to receive the message.
participantMessages.noRegistrationHere: This event takes no registrations on the site, so there is nobody to message from here.
participantMessages.testLine: Test registrations, which receive it too and are counted nowhere: {test}.
participantMessages.cost: Emails, the club's copies included: {messages} — taken from the Mailgun allowance ({allowance}).
participantMessages.deferredDay: {now} of them can go today; the other {deferred} stay in the queue and go by themselves after midnight (UTC), when the daily allowance comes back. None is lost.
participantMessages.deferredMonth: {now} of them can go this month; the other {deferred} stay in the queue and go by themselves when the monthly allowance comes back. None is lost.
participantMessages.subject: Subject
participantMessages.subjectHelp: In both languages, required, at most {max} characters each. You can use the fields {list}; they are filled in for each participant.
participantMessages.bodyHelp: In both languages, required, plain text, at most {max} characters each. A blank line starts a new paragraph. Fields filled in for each participant: {list} — the race number shows only for those who already have one. The event's date and place, the button to its page and the usual links come under the message by themselves.
participantMessages.bodyScope: Write only about this event: weather, place, time, safety, a change or a cancellation. No advertising, offers from sponsors or other businesses, and no other events: those would be commercial communications, or a purpose other than the one participants gave us their address for (Law no. 506/2004, art. 12; art. 5(1)(b) GDPR), and need each person's separate consent.
participantMessages.previewHelp: Exactly the email that goes out, for a sample participant, {name}, number {bibNumber}. It updates as you type.
participantMessages.previewUnavailable: The preview is not available right now. The message can still be sent.
participantMessages.previewUnknown: Unknown fields: {names}. The message cannot be sent with them — use only the fields listed under the boxes.
participantMessages.confirmBody: The email goes now, through the email queue, to each in their own language, and cannot be withdrawn.

sent.one: Message queued for {count} participant. It goes out in a few minutes.
sent.few: Message queued for {count} participants. It goes out in a few minutes.
sent.other: Message queued for {count} participants. It goes out in a few minutes.

participantMessages.duplicate: This message had already been sent, so nothing was queued a second time.
participantMessages.cancelledNote: The event is cancelled. The message still goes if you send it — to announce a new date, for instance.
participantMessages.seriesNote: This event is part of a series: the message goes only to those registered for this date. For another date, open it from the editor and send from there.
participantMessages.historyEmpty: No message sent from here for this event yet.

groupRunDeclarations.title: Signed declarations (group run)
groupRunDeclarations.help: Who signed the optional declaration on the run's page, and when. The email address is in the PDF; no identity document is asked for. The platform deletes the declarations {days} after the run.
groupRunDeclarations.reasonHelp: It stays in the club's log, with your name. Do not write the person's name.
groupRunDeclarations.eraseBody: The declaration and the messages about it are deleted for good. The log keeps your name and the reason, never the signer's.
groupRunDeclarations.erased: The declaration was erased. The log keeps your name and the reason.

newsletter.title: Subscribers
newsletter.intro: Who subscribed on the contact page and to which topics, what was sent and when. No address appears here, only the numbers.
newsletter.off: The contact page does not offer the subscription yet: the privacy notice in force does not describe the newsletter. Approve in /admin/legal a new notice started from the platform's text — the subscription appears by itself the day it takes effect.
newsletter.counts: Confirmed subscribers: {confirmed} · addresses not confirmed yet: {unconfirmed}
newsletter.allowanceNone: The email plan has no ceiling: the whole newsletter leaves now.
newsletter.allowanceDay: At most {count} newsletter emails can leave today: half the daily allowance stays for registrations. What does not fit leaves over the next days, by itself.
newsletter.allowanceMonth: At most {count} newsletter emails can leave this month: a fifth of the monthly allowance stays for registrations. What does not fit leaves after the reset, by itself.
newsletter.composeIntro: A message to the subscribers of one topic, in Romanian and in English: each receives it in their own language first, with the unsubscribe link.
newsletter.topicHelp: The subscribers of this topic receive it, and those who receive everything the club sends.
newsletter.bodyHelp: Plain text, at most {max} characters: a blank line starts a paragraph. No fields in braces — a newsletter has no name or event to put in them.
newsletter.confirmBody: Topic: {topic}. Each receives it in their own language first, with the unsubscribe link. Once sent it cannot be stopped.
newsletter.withdrawTitle: Remove an address at someone's request
newsletter.withdrawHelp: When someone writes to say they no longer want the news: type their address here. We find it and delete it, with anything still waiting to be sent to it.
newsletter.withdrawConfirmTitle: Remove the address from the newsletter?
newsletter.withdrawConfirmBody: The address is deleted from the news list, with the topics chosen. The person can subscribe again from the contact page.

sent.one: The newsletter was queued for {count} subscriber.
sent.few: The newsletter was queued for {count} subscribers.
sent.other: The newsletter was queued for {count} subscribers.

newsletter.duplicate: This newsletter had already been sent: nothing more was queued.
newsletter.withdrawn: The address was removed from the newsletter.
newsletter.notFound: The address was not on the newsletter.
newsletter.lastSendNone: Nothing sent to the subscribers yet.
newsletter.previewHelp: The message exactly as a subscriber receives it, from what the boxes hold now — with their unsubscribe link replaced by an example.
newsletter.previewUnavailable: The preview is not available right now. The message can still be sent.

Legal.unavailable: This document has not been published for this environment yet.
Legal.botCheckNotice: The “I'm not a robot” check is run by Cloudflare, which sees your IP address and browser details for that purpose only.

Registration.title: Register: {event}
Registration.listOptIn: I want to appear on the participant list
Registration.incompleteHint: Fill in the fields marked with * to send.
Registration.submittedAlready: If you were already registered for this event, that email is your existing confirmation — no second registration was created.

done.heading: Almost there!
done.lead: We have emailed you a link to confirm your place at {event}, {date}.

open.title: Open the email and press the link
open.body: That is all. The link is valid for {confirmation}.

declare.title: Sign the declaration
declare.body: From that same email: read it and type your name — online, or on paper at the registration desk on race day.
declare.bodyLater: The place is yours. We ask you to confirm {opens} before the start: sign the declaration online — or on paper, at the registration desk on race day. You can sign earlier, from the registration email.

confirmed.title: You are in
confirmed.body: You get the confirmation, with your QR code and race number. See you at the start!

done.delay: It usually arrives within a minute, five at the most.
done.notArrived: Not there? Look in Spam too. The link is valid for {confirmation}, so there is time.

deliveryNotice.capture: This is a development environment: no email is sent from here at all — messages can only be read in the backoffice. Do not wait for one in your inbox.
deliveryNotice.allowlist: This is the test environment: emails reach only the addresses the club has authorized. If yours is not among them, nothing will arrive — and that is not your fault.
deliveryNotice.everyone: This is the test site: emails really are sent from here, marked “[QA]” in the subject — but a registration made here is not a real one and holds no place in the race.

errors.title: The registration could not be submitted
errors.phone: The number is not valid. Type only the digits of the number, without the country code (that is chosen on the left).
errors.emergencySame: The emergency contact needs a different number from yours — nobody can ring your own phone if something happens to you.
errors.tooYoung: The minimum age for this event is {age} on the day of the race.
errors.captcha: The anti-bot check did not pass. Tick the box again and resend.
errors.generic: The registration could not be submitted. Check what you entered and try again.
errors.throttledTitle: You have already sent this form a few times
errors.databaseAwayTitle: We could not reach our records just now
errors.databaseAway: Nothing was registered and no email is on its way. Everything you filled in is still below — try again in a few minutes. If it keeps happening, the site may be paused for a while; the event page says until when.
errors.throttled: We have had several registrations from this address in the last hour, so we have paused it for a while. Try again in an hour — or, if it is urgent, write to us through the contact form and we will register you ourselves. Nothing you filled in has been lost.
errors.tooFast: The automated check did not pass first time — it happens to real people too. Your answers are still here.
errors.tooFastNothingSent: Nothing was registered and no email was sent to you. Press “Send the registration again” — your answers and your ticks are still here.
errors.waitlistFullNothingSent: Nothing was registered and no email was sent. What you filled in is still in the form.

Registration.displayNameHelp: By default the participant list and the results show your full name. If you would rather they showed something else — “Ana P.”, for instance — write it here. To stay off the list entirely, use the option below.
Registration.birthDateHelp: The minimum age is {age} on the day of the race. Age categories are worked out against that day too.
Registration.birthDateHelpNoMinimum: Age categories are worked out against the day of the race.

ageRule.minimumAndGuardian: Minimum age: {age}. Under 18, a parent or legal guardian registers the runner, with their consent.
ageRule.guardianOnly: Under 18, a parent or legal guardian registers the runner, with their consent.

Registration.sexHelp: For category rankings; you may choose “Prefer not to say”.
Registration.originHelp: Optional. Tells the club where its events' participants come from.
Registration.preferredLocale: The language for your emails and the declaration
Registration.preferredLocaleHelp: Emails come in both languages; this one first. You sign the declaration in the language you choose.
Registration.phoneHelp: The number without the country code — for example 0712 345 678.
Registration.emergencyContactHelp: Tell this person you gave us their name and number: we call only if something happens to you at the race. We keep them as long as the registration.
Registration.healthNotesHelp: Only what an organizer would need to know if you needed help on race day. You may leave this empty.
Registration.healthConsent: I agree that the race organizers may keep this health information, only for my safety on race day. I can withdraw it at any time from “My registrations”.
Registration.displayNameToggle: Want to appear publicly under a different name?

fieldNames.fitnessDeclared: The statement that you are medically fit
fieldNames.emailConfirm: The address typed a second time
fieldNames.fitnessAcknowledged: The acknowledgement about the person's fitness statement

Registration.requiredLegend: Fields marked * are required. Everything else is optional — leave it blank if you would rather not say.

resend.title: Send the registration link again
resend.intro: If our message did not arrive, enter the address you registered with and we will send the link again. Check your spam folder too.
resend.emailHelp: The address you used when registering.
resend.sent: If that address has a registration, we have just sent the link there. Check your spam folder too.
resend.stillNothing: Nothing arrived even after asking again?
resend.contactLinkLabel: Write to us and we will register you

form.title: Fill in the form
form.body: Your name, email, phone and an emergency contact. It takes a minute.

email.title: Confirm your email address
email.body: You get a link. Open it within {confirmation} — otherwise the registration expires and the place stays free.

declaration.title: Sign the declaration
declaration.body: From that same email, read the declaration and type your name — online, or on paper at the registration desk on race day. The registration is complete only with the signed declaration. Your place is held for {hold}; if a waiting list forms, after that it goes to the next in line.
declaration.bodyLater: The place is yours, but the race is free, so we ask for a confirmation: {opens} before the start you get an email and sign the declaration of own responsibility — online, or on paper at the registration desk on race day. You can sign earlier, from the registration email. If a waiting list forms, the place is held for you until {due}; after that it goes to the next in line.
declaration.bodyLaterAtStart: The place is yours, but the race is free, so we ask for a confirmation: you can sign the declaration of own responsibility from now, from the registration email, any time until the start — online, or on paper at the registration desk on race day. {opens} before the start we send you a reminder email. The place does not lapse before the start.

confirmed.title: You are in
confirmed.body: You get the confirmation email, with your QR code and race number. We send a reminder {reminder} before the start.
confirmed.bodyNoReminder: You get the confirmation email, with your QR code and race number.

raceDay.title: On race day
raceDay.body: Show the QR code (or say your name) at the registration desk and collect your number.

waitingList.title: If it is full
waitingList.body: You join the waiting list, in order of registration. When a place frees up, you get an offer by email and {offer} to sign the declaration.

family.title: Registering someone else on the same address?
family.body: Send the form again with the person's full name and birth date — you get an email where you confirm with one button.

now.details: Fill in the form. We will then email you to confirm your address.
now.confirm: We have sent you a confirmation link.
now.declare: One step left: read and sign the declaration — here, or on paper at the registration desk on race day. Your place is held. Once you sign, we email you the signed declaration (PDF) and your race number — usually within a few minutes, within the hour at the latest.
now.done: Your registration is confirmed. See you at the start!

disclosure.guardian: Registering a minor — parent or legal guardian

Registration.clubMemberDeclared: I am a member of the {club} group
Registration.clubNameFromMembership: Filled in because you ticked that you are a member. Untick it to enter a different club.
Registration.socialsHelp: Optional. Used only to follow you and tag you in the club's posts; a tag is public on that network. Never shown on the site. You can delete them at any time from “My registrations”.
Registration.stravaUrlHelp: From the Strava app: Profile → Share → copy the link.
Registration.guardianHelp: A participant under 18 is registered by a parent or legal guardian, who also signs the declaration of own responsibility on their behalf and collects the kit. You fill in the child's details and give the choices below (public list, health information) on their behalf. The email and phone may be yours. For an adult, leave this empty.
Registration.guardianName: Full name of the parent / guardian
Registration.guardianNameHelp: Required under 18. This name appears on the declaration as the signer.
Registration.privacyBanner: Nothing you write here appears on the site. The club uses it only to run the race: the organizing team and the providers that host the site and send the emails see it. The signed declaration is emailed to you, and a copy, with your identity document's series and number masked (at most the first two and last two characters remain), goes to the club's archive. We keep the registration for three years after the event.
Registration.privacyBannerWithList: Nothing you write here appears on the site — with one exception: this event has a public participant list, and your name and the club you wrote go on it, only if you tick the box below. Without the tick, once you are confirmed you are only counted, as “Participant (name hidden)”. Nothing else is published: not your email, not your phone, not your date of birth. The club uses your details only to run the race: the organizing team and the providers that host the site and send the emails see them. The signed declaration is emailed to you, and a copy, with your identity document's series and number masked (at most the first two and last two characters remain), goes to the club's archive. We keep the registration for three years after the event.
Registration.contactNote: Confidential. Used only to reach you, and to call somebody if something happens to you during the event.
Registration.healthIntro: Optional, and only if you want to. Write only what the race organizers should know if you need help — an allergy, a treatment, a condition. Only the organizers see it; it is deleted seven days after the event.
Registration.fitnessDeclared: I declare on my own responsibility that I am medically fit to take part.
Registration.clubMemberHint: I have been to at least 3 group runs in the past year.

rules.reading: Press the box or the button: the conditions open here, you read them to the end, and only then is the box ticked.
rules.tick: I have read and agree to the race conditions
rules.missing: The race conditions — open them and read to the end
rules.keepReading: Scroll to the end to be able to confirm.
rules.agreeButton: I have read them and I agree
rules.agreed: You have read the race conditions and agree to them.
rules.plain: I have read and agree to the race conditions:
rules.plainPage: I have read and agree to the race conditions, on

Registration.phoneInvalid: That does not look like a complete number for the country chosen — check the digits.
Registration.emailMismatch: The two addresses are not the same — check the letters.
Registration.emailNoPaste: Type the address here by hand — copying it from the box above would check nothing.
Registration.emailAllowPaste: Cannot type it? Paste it anyway
Registration.emailInvalid: That does not look like an email address. Check the letters and the @.
Registration.emailHelp: This is where the confirmation link goes. Type it carefully.
Registration.phoneTooShort: Keep going — a number has at least 4 digits.
Registration.phoneValid: Looks right. We will store it as
Registration.botCheckWait: One second while we check you are not a robot — we send the form ourselves as soon as it answers; no need to press again.
Registration.submitSlow: This is taking longer than usual. Give it a few more seconds and do not press again — a second press would only queue behind the first.
Registration.listOptInStates: The list also shows where your registration stands: “{pending}” once your address is confirmed, “{waitlisted}” while you wait for a place, and “{confirmed}” after the declaration. A cancelled registration does not appear.

another.linkGone: This link for another person is no longer used. Send the form below again with your address and the person's full name and birth date: you get an email where you confirm their registration with one button.

terms.accept: I have read and accept the <terms>Terms and conditions</terms> (version {version}), including, expressly, the clauses on the club cancelling or changing an event, being stopped or excluded on the course, the limits of the club's liability, the governing law and the competent court.
terms.missing: We cannot take registrations just now: the club has no approved terms and conditions yet. Please come back soon.
terms.changed: The terms and conditions changed while you were filling in the form. Read the version named below and tick the box again.

Registration.restingForm: The form is paused while we cannot check our records — it cannot be sent right now. Whatever you have filled in stays here; come back in a few minutes.

Registrations.invalidOrExpired: This link is no longer valid. We can send you a new one, to the same email address.
Registrations.cancelKeepsRecord: Cancelling frees your place; we keep the registration for three years as a record. Want to see, correct or erase your data? <contact>Write to us</contact>.

confirm.title: Confirm your email address
confirm.prompt: We are confirming your email address. If nothing happens in a few seconds, press the button.
confirm.done: Your email address has been confirmed.
confirm.eventOff: The event has been cancelled or is over, so the registration does not go on: no place was held for you and there is nothing you need to do.
confirm.waitlistFull: The places and the waiting list are full, so your address was not confirmed and nothing was held for you. The link in your email stays valid for {confirmation} from when you sent the form: if a place opens on the waiting list in the meantime, open it again.
confirm.noWaitlist: Every place has been taken and the event has no waiting list, so your address was not confirmed and nothing was held for you. The link in your email stays valid for {confirmation} from when you sent the form: if a place frees up in the meantime, open it again.

declare.title: Event declaration
declare.accept: I have read and accept the declaration above, including, expressly, the limitation of the organiser's liability to the extent the law allows.
declare.signPersonally: {participant} must sign this declaration personally. If this email address is not theirs, forward them the link or hand them the phone: nobody signs for another adult.
declare.typedName: Type your full name as a signature
declare.changed: The declaration was updated while you were reading it. Nothing was recorded. Below is the current text — please read it and sign again.
declare.waitlistFull: The deadline to sign had passed and your place goes to somebody on the waiting list. We could not put you back on the list, because it is full too, so the signature was not recorded.
declare.noWaitlist: The deadline to sign had passed and your place goes to somebody who was waiting for it. The event has no waiting list and no free places left, so the signature was not recorded.
declare.doneWaitlisted: The place was no longer available; you have been added to the waiting list.
declare.deadline: Your place is held until {deadline}. With no waiting list it stays yours after that, until the start — but the registration is complete only with the signed declaration.
declare.deadlineAtStart: Your place is held until the start, {deadline}: it does not lapse before. The registration is complete only with the signed declaration.
declare.deadlinePassed: The {deadline} deadline has passed, but the place is still yours: sign now and the registration is complete.
declare.idDocumentHelp: Your identity card — for example “BV 123456” — or your passport if you are from abroad. It goes into the declaration; the kit is collected against it. The series and number are deleted from our database seven days after the event and are masked in the club's copy (at most the first two and last two characters remain); we never keep a copy of the document.
declare.typedNameHelp: Type the full name you registered with. It appears as a signature.
nextConfirmed: The confirmation email is on its way, with your QR code and your access code — keep it for race day.
You get a reminder {reminder} before the start, with the time, the place, what to bring and, if assigned, your race number.
If you can no longer come, cancel from the link in the email: your place goes to somebody on the waiting list.
nextWaitlisted: You are on the waiting list; if a place frees up, you get an email with a confirmation link.
The link has a deadline; if you do not confirm in time, the place moves on.
You can withdraw at any time from the email you received.
declare.pressFailed: We could not record the signature. Tick that you have read the declaration and try again — your link is fine.
declare.idDocumentTypeHelp: Choose the kind of document — it appears in the declaration with the series and number.
declare.typedNameHelpWithName: You registered as {name} — type exactly this name. It appears as a signature.
declare.typedNameHelpForMinor: A parent or legal guardian of the minor {participant} signs, with the name given at registration: {name} — type exactly this name. It appears as a signature.
declare.signatureMismatch: The signature must be exactly the name you registered with: {name}.
declare.signatureMismatchForMinor: The signature must be exactly the parent or guardian name given at registration: {name}.
declare.signatureMismatchRich: The signature must be exactly the name you registered with: {name}.
declare.signatureMismatchForMinorRich: The signature must be exactly the parent or guardian name given at registration: {name}.
declare.signatureNameWrong: If the name given at registration is wrong, <contact>write to us</contact>: the club corrects it, and you then sign from the same link.
declare.signatureNameWrongReply: If the name given at registration is wrong, reply to the email you received or <contact>write to us</contact>: the club corrects it, and you then sign from the same link.
declare.signatureNameWrongForMinor: If the parent or guardian name given at registration is wrong, it cannot be changed on this registration: cancel it from <mine>My registrations</mine> (or <contact>write to us</contact> and the club cancels it), then register the minor again with the right name. The new registration gets a place like any other, or a place on the waiting list if the race has filled up by then.
declare.signatureNameWrongForMinorReply: If the parent or guardian name given at registration is wrong, it cannot be changed on this registration: cancel it from <mine>My registrations</mine> (or reply to the email you received, or <contact>write to us</contact>, and the club cancels it), then register the minor again with the right name. The new registration gets a place like any other, or a place on the waiting list if the race has filled up by then.
declare.nameRefusedTitle: The signature does not match the name given at registration
declare.nameRefusedNothingRecorded: Nothing was recorded and your link is fine: correct the name and sign again.
declare.documentRefusedTitle: An identity document is missing or not written correctly
declare.documentRefusedNothingRecorded: Nothing was recorded and your link is fine: type the document's series and number, for example “BV 123456”, and sign again.
declare.twoSignersIntro: A minor participant's declaration is signed by two people: the minor and the parent or legal guardian. Each gives their identity document and types their name, below.
declare.minorIdDocumentType: Which document the minor will show
declare.minorIdDocument: The minor's identity document (series and number)
declare.minorIdDocumentHelp: The minor's identity card — for example “BV 123456” — or passport. It goes into the declaration, beside the parent's or guardian's.
declare.guardianIdDocumentType: Which document the parent or guardian will show
declare.guardianIdDocument: The parent's or guardian's identity document (series and number)
declare.minorTypedNameHelp: The minor signs too, with the name they were registered under: {name} — type exactly this name. It appears as a signature.
declare.minorSignatureMismatch: The minor's signature must be exactly the name they were registered under: {name}.
declare.minorSignatureMismatchRich: The minor's signature must be exactly the name they were registered under: {name}.
declare.minorNameWrong: If the minor's name given at registration is wrong, <contact>write to us</contact>: the club corrects it, and you then sign from the same link.
declare.minorNameWrongReply: If the minor's name given at registration is wrong, reply to the email you received or <contact>write to us</contact>: the club corrects it, and you then sign from the same link.

list.title: The public participant list
list.listed: Your name appears on this event's public participant list.
list.notListed: Your name does not appear on this event's public participant list.
list.help: The list shows the name (or the display name you chose) and the club, and only on events where the club publishes one; without your name, you are only counted, as “Participant (name hidden)”. The choice is yours and you can change it at any time: here, from the confirmation email or from "My registrations".
list.optOut: Take me off the public list
list.optIn: Show my name on the public list
list.changedHelp: The link from the email has been used. This page carries a fresh one — if you change your mind, press the button above.
list.failed: Could not save your choice. Try again or write to us.
list.shortListed: You are on the public participant list.
list.shortNotListed: You are not on the public participant list.

withdraw.title: What you gave us with your consent
withdraw.help: The health note and your Strava and Instagram accounts are here only because you chose to give them. You can delete them here at any time; your registration and your place stay as they are.
withdraw.healthDone: Your health note and its consent are deleted.
withdraw.socialsDone: Your Strava link and Instagram username are deleted.
withdraw.failed: We could not delete it. Try again or write to us.

mine.title: My registrations
mine.intro: Type the address you registered with and we send one link to every active registration of yours — the state of each, the access code and QR, and the option to withdraw.
mine.sent: If that address has registrations, we have just sent the link there. Check the spam folder too.
mine.empty: You have no active registration at the moment.
mine.bibProvisional: Provisional number. It is settled when registration closes, and you get it by email then.
mine.cancelled: Your place has been released. This link is spent; for another change, ask for a new one.
mine.closedHelp: These registrations are no longer active, but they still hold details you gave us only because you agreed to. You can delete them here; the rest of the registration is kept for as long as the privacy notice says.
mine.eventCancelled: The event has been cancelled. Your registration stays with us as a record, with the status above, and there is nothing you need to do.
mine.confirmBy: Confirm by signing the declaration, from the registration email, by {due}. Or on paper, at the registration desk, on race day.

manage.title: Manage your registration
manage.prompt: You can cancel this registration. The place will be released immediately.
manage.eventStarted: This event has already started; the registration can no longer be cancelled.
manage.codeIntro: Show this code at the number pickup desk. It is in your confirmation email too.
manage.selfCheckIn: I have arrived — mark me as here
manage.selfCheckInHelp: You can do this from {checkin} before the start. You still pick up your number at the desk.
manage.selfCheckInDone: You are marked as here. Pick up your number at the desk.
manage.selfCheckInFailed: Could not mark you as here. Tell the desk; they will sort it out.

spent.resendHelp: A link from an email works once, so this one no longer opens anything. If you need the next step, we can send it to the same address again.
spent.registerAgainHelp: If you change your mind, you can register again from the event page.
spent.waitHelp: There is nothing for you to do now. If a place opens up, you will get an email with a confirmation link.

CONFIRM_EMAIL.title: One step left: confirming your address
CONFIRM_EMAIL.body: This link has already been used, but your registration is still waiting for your email address to be confirmed.

SIGN_DECLARATION.title: Your address is confirmed — the declaration is next
SIGN_DECLARATION.body: This link did its job and does not open a second time. Your place is held, and the registration is complete once you sign the declaration — its own link was emailed to you.

WAITLISTED.title: You are on the waiting list
WAITLISTED.body: This link has already been used. Your registration is in the event's waiting list.

CONFIRMED.title: Your registration is confirmed
CONFIRMED.body: This link has already been used and opens nothing more — but it does not need to: you have a place in the race. Your check-in code and QR code are in the confirmation email.

CANCELLED.title: This registration was cancelled
CANCELLED.body: This link was used to cancel. The place was released and the registration is no longer active.

LAPSED.title: This registration is no longer active
LAPSED.body: This link has already been used, and the registration has lapsed since — either the deadline passed or the event started.

family.title: Registering one more person
family.intro: The registration form for {event} was sent again from the address {email}, for another person. We have not registered them yet: check the details below and confirm.
family.next: Once confirmed, the person has their own place and receives at {email} their own email with the declaration to sign, then their own QR code. One address may register at most {people} for an event.

values.capture: Nothing is transmitted. Messages are held in memory — which on a deployed serverless host means they reach nobody at all, so registration looks broken to anyone but a developer.
values.allowlist: Real delivery, but only to the addresses in EMAIL_ALLOWLIST; everything else is captured. This is what a Mailgun sandbox domain is, and it is how a small closed group tests the whole journey safely.
values.live: Real delivery to whoever registered. Permitted only when APP_ENV is production; stating it anywhere else fails at startup.

Devs.operationalTitle: What each limit does when it is met
Devs.operationalIntro: Who stops you — the provider's own API, or this application's code — what the application does at that moment, and which variable or monitor is involved. Costs and plans are not here: they live on /admin/tasks, for the people who pay the invoice.

mailgunDaily.title: Mailgun's daily allowance (100 messages on the free plan)
mailgunDaily.body: Mailgun refuses the send with the same HTTP 400 it uses for a malformed message. The adapter recognises the limit wording, classifies the refusal as throttled, and the outbox row stays PENDING with its next attempt scheduled just after midnight UTC — not the ordinary backoff, which would spend all six attempts within an hour and mark a good message FAILED. The signal is the email-volume figure above; there is no configuration variable for the cap.

captureOnServerless.title: Capture mode delivers nothing on a deployed environment
captureOnServerless.body: The capture adapter holds messages in the process's memory, and on serverless hosting the process is gone before anybody could read the link. A colleague who is not on the allowlist registers and then simply never hears anything. Allowlist mode with a real provider is the only way somebody outside the code completes a registration.

schedulerFloor.title: The cadence of the scheduled jobs
schedulerFloor.body: Vercel Hobby allows one run a day and refuses a finer expression at deploy time, so the scheduler is the GitHub Actions workflow plus an external pinger; GitHub's own minimum is five minutes, and measured here the real cadence is roughly two hours. The application does not break in between: hold expiry is evaluated inside every capacity transaction (§10.6), so a late run delays a message rather than overbooking an event. Both endpoints are guarded by JOB_SECRET, and each job's liveness is reported below and in /api/health.

hobbyCapPause.title: Exceeding a Hobby cap pauses the feature for 30 days
hobbyCapPause.body: Not a bill — an outage with a fixed sentence, and you cannot buy your way out of it during the window. There is nothing the application can do at that point; the only response is to upgrade before the window. It is visible only in the Vercel dashboard — nothing here reports it.

identityDomain.title: Zitadel Free: zero custom domains, one administrator
identityDomain.body: No effect on the code, but it decides which host staff sign in on. While STAFF_AUTH_MODE=provider runs on the provider's hostname the limit is not felt; on the club's own domain it needs a paid tier. STAFF_AUTH_MODE=disabled answers 404 to every staff route, which is what an environment with no tenant should do.

statementTimeout.title: statement_timeout 10s and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 30s
statementTimeout.body: Enforced by this application rather than by Neon: db/client.ts sets both on the pool. The risk was never the connection count (max: 10 is per warm instance, and PgBouncer accepts far more) but one unbounded query holding a Vercel function for 300 seconds. The first timeout is enforced by PostgreSQL, so it holds even when the Node process is frozen; the second covers an instance killed between two statements of an open transaction. There is no connection timeout, deliberately: on Neon Free the first request after an idle period waits for the database to wake.

sent.title: Check your inbox
sent.body: If the address is right, within a few minutes you receive an email with a link. The subscription starts only once you press it. Can't find it? Look in the Spam folder too.

errors.title: The subscription has not started yet
errors.consent: Tick the consent: without it we cannot send you the news.
errors.captcha: The anti-robot check did not pass. Tick it again and send.
errors.limited: You have already asked a few times in the last hour. Check your inbox (and the Spam folder) or try again later.
errors.unavailable: Subscribing to the news is not available right now. Try again later.

Newsletter.linkInvalid: This link is no longer valid

confirm.title: Confirm your subscription
confirm.intro: Press the button to start receiving the club's news at {email}.
confirm.doneBody: We write to you only about the topics you chose. From the link in every email you change them or unsubscribe.
confirm.invalidBody: It may have been used already, expired, or you have asked for another since. To get a new one, subscribe again from the contact page.

manage.title: Your subscription to the news
manage.intro: You receive the club's news at {email}.
manage.saved: We saved what you want to receive.
manage.topicsRefused: Choose at least one topic — or, if you want nothing more, unsubscribe below.
manage.unsubscribeBody: We take you off the list and delete your address. You receive no more news emails; your event registrations are not touched.
manage.goneBody: We deleted your address from the news list. You can come back at any time from the contact page.
manage.invalidBody: It has expired or the subscription no longer exists. Every new email from us carries a new link; you can also subscribe again from the contact page.
